note: Hand-authored per-sentence analysis for the Toen topic: a single past occasion or period (toen), and toen as the adverb then. Status ai-editorial-checked is not native-speaker review.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Coming home yesterday happened once, so the past conjunction 'toen' fits where 'als' (repeated) would not.

pat-toen-01.situationNl: Gisteren kwam je moe terug van je werk. Je deed iets voor een vriendin. Vertel wat je op dat moment deed.
pat-toen-01.situationEn: Yesterday you came home and phoned Zoë. Say this in one sentence that ties the two moments together.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The separable verb 'thuiskomen' rejoins at the end of the toen-clause: 'thuiskwam', not 'kwam ... thuis'.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The toen-clause fills the first slot, so the finite verb 'belde' comes next and the subject 'ik' follows it.

pat-toen-01.meaning: When I got home, I called Zoë.
pat-toen-01.order: The comma separates two clauses. In the first the verb is last, in the second the verb comes first. Reading the sentence aloud, listen for the pause after 'thuiskwam'.
pat-toen-01.forms: thuiskomen: ik kom thuis (main clause), toen ik thuiskwam (dependent, past). bellen > belde. The name Zoë keeps its diaeresis.
pat-toen-01.compare: English 'When I got home, I called Zoë' has the same order of events. Dutch changes the verb position in both clauses and keeps the particle 'thuis' attached to its verb.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik kwam thuis, belde ik Zoë.
mistakes.right: Toen ik thuiskwam, belde ik Zoë.
mistakes.why: In a toen-clause a separable verb stays in one piece at the end: 'thuiskwam'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik thuiskwam, ik belde Zoë.
mistakes.right: Toen ik thuiskwam, belde ik Zoë.
mistakes.why: After the opening clause the main verb comes first: 'belde ik'. Keeping 'ik' first breaks the verb-second rule.

contrast.dutch: Ik kwam thuis en belde Zoë.
contrast.english: I came home and called Zoë.
contrast.note: Joined with 'en', the two actions become a plain sequence; 'toen' instead marks the exact moment.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Opening the file was a single act yesterday, and the error followed at that moment, so 'toen' marks it.

pat-toen-02.situationNl: Gisteren probeerde je een document te bekijken. Er ging iets mis op het scherm. Vertel wat je zag en wat de aanleiding was.
pat-toen-02.situationEn: You opened a file yesterday and an error message appeared. Say how the two events are connected.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The object 'het bestand' stands before the finite verb 'opende', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: een foutmelding
clauses.why: The finite verb 'verscheen' leads the main clause; the placeholder 'er' fills the subject slot before the real subject 'een foutmelding'.

pat-toen-02.meaning: When I opened the file, an error message appeared.
pat-toen-02.order: The toen-clause names the trigger, the main clause names the consequence. 'Er' appears because the real subject 'een foutmelding' is new information and stays behind the verb.
pat-toen-02.forms: openen > opende. verschijnen > verscheen (strong verb). 'Foutmelding' is a de-word, a compound of fout and melding.
pat-toen-02.compare: English 'an error message appeared' starts with the subject. Dutch often uses 'er' to introduce a new subject after the verb.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik opende het bestand, verscheen er een foutmelding.
mistakes.right: Toen ik het bestand opende, verscheen er een foutmelding.
mistakes.why: The object goes before the finite verb 'opende' at the end of the toen-clause.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik het bestand opende, een foutmelding verscheen.
mistakes.right: Toen ik het bestand opende, verscheen er een foutmelding.
mistakes.why: The main clause after the comma has the verb first; with a new subject Dutch adds 'er'.

contrast.dutch: Bij het openen van het bestand verscheen er een foutmelding.
contrast.english: On opening the file, an error message appeared.
contrast.note: A noun phrase replaces the clause, so the main clause needs no inversion by a conjunction.

sense.label: toen = when (a past period)
sense.why: Being at the office was a stretch of time yesterday; 'toen' places the conversation inside it.

pat-toen-03.situationNl: Gisteren was je een hele dag op je werkplek. Je had daar een belangrijk gesprek. Vertel met wie en waar je was.
pat-toen-03.situationEn: You were at the office yesterday and spoke with your manager there. Say it in one connected sentence.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The place phrase 'op kantoor' stands before the finite verb 'was', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: After the toen-clause the finite verb 'sprak' comes first, then the subject 'ik' and the phrase 'met mijn manager'.

pat-toen-03.meaning: When I was at the office, I spoke with my manager.
pat-toen-03.order: Two clauses: the first sets the scene with the verb 'was' at its end, the second tells the event with 'sprak' first. 'Spreken met' takes the preposition 'met'.
pat-toen-03.forms: zijn > was. spreken > sprak (strong). 'Mijn manager' is a de-word. 'Op kantoor' needs no article.
pat-toen-03.compare: English 'spoke with my manager' is the same, but English keeps 'was' before 'at the office'. Dutch puts it behind.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik was op kantoor, sprak ik met mijn manager.
mistakes.right: Toen ik op kantoor was, sprak ik met mijn manager.
mistakes.why: The finite verb belongs at the end of the toen-clause, after 'op kantoor'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik op kantoor was, ik sprak met mijn manager.
mistakes.right: Toen ik op kantoor was, sprak ik met mijn manager.
mistakes.why: After the comma the finite verb must come first: 'sprak ik', not 'ik sprak'.

contrast.dutch: Ik sprak met mijn manager op kantoor.
contrast.english: I spoke with my manager at the office.
contrast.note: Without 'toen', the same facts become one main clause with the place at the end.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The visit being described is one earlier occasion, so 'toen' (not 'als') connects arrival and closed shop.

pat-toen-04.situationNl: Vorige keer ging je naar een kleine zaak in de buurt en stond je voor een verrassing. Beschrijf wat je zag bij je komst.
pat-toen-04.situationEn: On your last visit you arrived at a small shop and found something surprising. Describe what you saw on arrival.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The separable verb 'aankomen' rejoins at the end: 'aankwam'. The clause is just subject and verb.

clauses.subject: de winkel
clauses.why: The finite verb 'was' comes first after the comma, then the subject 'de winkel' and the predicate 'dicht'.

pat-toen-04.meaning: When I arrived, the shop was closed.
pat-toen-04.order: The shortest possible pattern: a two-word toen-clause, then verb, subject, predicate. 'Dicht' stays at the end of the main clause.
pat-toen-04.forms: aankomen: ik kom aan, ik kwam aan, toen ik aankwam. 'Dicht zijn' = to be closed. 'Winkel' is a de-word.
pat-toen-04.compare: English 'When I arrived' has the same shape. Dutch separable verbs rejoin: 'aankwam' where the main clause would split 'kwam ... aan'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik kwam aan, was de winkel dicht.
mistakes.right: Toen ik aankwam, was de winkel dicht.
mistakes.why: In a toen-clause the separable verb is not split.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik aankwam, de winkel was dicht.
mistakes.right: Toen ik aankwam, was de winkel dicht.
mistakes.why: After the comma the verb 'was' must come first.

contrast.dutch: Ik kwam aan en de winkel was dicht.
contrast.english: I arrived and the shop was closed.
contrast.note: With 'en' both halves are main clauses with the verb second, and the link in time is lost.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The start of yesterday's meeting is one moment; 'toen' ties your readiness to it.

pat-toen-05.situationNl: Gisteren begon een belangrijk overleg precies op tijd. Jij had je voorbereid. Vertel hoe het er voor jou op dat moment voorstond.
pat-toen-05.situationEn: Yesterday an important meeting began on time and you were prepared. Say how things stood for you at that moment.

clauses.subject: de vergadering
clauses.why: The subject 'de vergadering' comes first and the finite verb 'begon' closes the clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The finite verb 'zat' leads the main clause, then the subject 'ik', then 'al klaar'.

pat-toen-05.meaning: When the meeting started, I was already sitting ready.
pat-toen-05.order: 'Zat ... klaar' (sat ready) expresses being prepared in a seated position. 'Al' shows that the readiness came earlier than the start.
pat-toen-05.forms: zitten > zat. beginnen > begon. 'Klaar zitten' = to be seated and ready.
pat-toen-05.compare: English says 'was already ready'. Dutch pictures the posture: 'zat al klaar'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de vergadering begon, ik zat al klaar.
mistakes.right: Toen de vergadering begon, zat ik al klaar.
mistakes.why: The main clause starts with the finite verb: 'zat ik'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen begon de vergadering, zat ik al klaar.
mistakes.right: Toen de vergadering begon, zat ik al klaar.
mistakes.why: In a toen-clause the verb is last: 'de vergadering begon'.

contrast.dutch: De vergadering begon, en ik zat al klaar.
contrast.english: The meeting started, and I was already sitting ready.
contrast.note: Two main clauses joined by 'en' state the facts without making one the frame for the other.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: One test of the connection yesterday gave one result, so 'toen' fits.

pat-toen-06.situationNl: Gisteren controleerde je of het netwerk in orde was. Dat was een enkele controle. Vertel wat daarbij bleek.
pat-toen-06.situationEn: You tested the connection once yesterday. Say what the result was, linking the test and the result.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The object 'de verbinding' stands before the finite verb 'testte', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: alles
clauses.why: After the comma the finite verb 'werkte' comes first and the subject 'alles' follows.

pat-toen-06.meaning: When I tested the connection, everything worked.
pat-toen-06.order: The result clause is very short because 'alles' (everything) is a compact subject. The verb 'werkte' is placed first by the inversion rule.
pat-toen-06.forms: testen > testte (the past of a verb with stem ending in t takes -te). werken > werkte. 'Alles' takes a singular verb.
pat-toen-06.compare: English 'everything worked' keeps subject then verb. Dutch swaps them after the opening clause.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik testte de verbinding, werkte alles.
mistakes.right: Toen ik de verbinding testte, werkte alles.
mistakes.why: The finite verb goes behind the object at the end of the toen-clause.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik de verbinding testte, alles werkte.
mistakes.right: Toen ik de verbinding testte, werkte alles.
mistakes.why: The main clause begins with its verb: 'werkte alles'.

contrast.dutch: Alles werkte toen ik de verbinding testte.
contrast.english: Everything worked when I tested the connection.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, there is no inversion; the toen-clause ends the sentence.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Waking up is one moment, so 'toen' links it to the weather at that moment.

pat-toen-07.situationNl: Je opende vanochtend je ogen en keek naar buiten. Beschrijf wat het weer deed op dat moment.
pat-toen-07.situationEn: Describe what the weather was like at the moment you opened your eyes this morning.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: 'Wakker werd' (became awake): the predicate 'wakker' stands before the finite verb 'werd', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: het
clauses.why: The finite verb 'regende' leads the main clause and the weather subject 'het' follows it.

pat-toen-07.meaning: When I woke up, it was raining.
pat-toen-07.order: 'Wakker worden' means to wake up (become awake). The weather clause uses the dummy subject 'het': 'regende het'.
pat-toen-07.forms: worden > werd. regenen > regende. 'Het regent' has no real subject; 'het' is only a placeholder.
pat-toen-07.compare: English 'it was raining' uses a continuous form. Dutch simply says 'regende het'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik werd wakker, regende het.
mistakes.right: Toen ik wakker werd, regende het.
mistakes.why: The predicate 'wakker' goes before the verb 'werd' at the end.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik wakker werd, het regende.
mistakes.right: Toen ik wakker werd, regende het.
mistakes.why: After the comma the verb comes first: 'regende het'.

contrast.dutch: Het regende toen ik wakker werd.
contrast.english: It was raining when I woke up.
contrast.note: With the main clause first the weather leads and the toen-clause closes the sentence.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The group's arrival at the station happened once, so 'toen' is the right conjunction.

pat-toen-08.situationNl: Jullie stapten uit de trein op een drukke dag. Beschrijf hoe het eruitzag bij het binnenkomen van de hal.
pat-toen-08.situationEn: Describe how crowded things were at the moment you and your group arrived at the station.

clauses.subject: wij
clauses.why: The plural separable verb 'aankomen' rejoins as 'aankwamen' at the end of the clause.

clauses.subject: het station
clauses.why: The finite verb 'was' leads the main clause, then 'het station' and the predicate 'vol'.

pat-toen-08.meaning: When we arrived, the station was full.
pat-toen-08.order: Plural 'wij' needs the plural past 'aankwamen' (not 'aankwam'). The main clause describes the scene with 'was ... vol'.
pat-toen-08.forms: aankomen > aankwam (singular) / aankwamen (plural). 'Station' is a het-word.
pat-toen-08.compare: English 'we arrived' does not change with the subject in the past. Dutch past tense has a different plural form.

mistakes.wrong: Toen wij aankwam, was het station vol.
mistakes.right: Toen wij aankwamen, was het station vol.
mistakes.why: The plural subject 'wij' needs the plural 'aankwamen'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen wij aankwamen, het station was vol.
mistakes.right: Toen wij aankwamen, was het station vol.
mistakes.why: After the comma the main clause opens with 'was', the verb of 'het station was vol'.

contrast.dutch: Bij onze aankomst was het station vol.
contrast.english: On our arrival the station was full.
contrast.note: A noun phrase replaces the clause; the main clause still starts with its verb.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: A friend's call came at one moment while a longer activity was going on; 'toen' marks the moment of interruption.

pat-toen-09.situationNl: Je stond vorige week in de keuken met pannen op het vuur. Er gebeurde iets via je telefoon. Vertel wat je deed en wat je stoorde.
pat-toen-09.situationEn: Say what you were busy with in the kitchen last week and who disturbed you.

clauses.subject: Hij
clauses.why: Hij is first, so 'belde' is second; the object 'mij' follows.

clauses.text: toen ik aan het koken was
clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The construction 'aan het koken' (busy cooking) stands before the finite verb 'was', which closes the clause.

pat-toen-09.meaning: He phoned me while I was cooking.
pat-toen-09.order: The imperfect 'was' plus 'aan het koken' shows an ongoing activity, interrupted by the shorter act 'belde'. The main clause comes first, so there is no inversion.
pat-toen-09.forms: bellen > belde. koken > aan het koken zijn (progressive). 'Mij' is the stressed object form.
pat-toen-09.compare: English 'was cooking' is a continuous. Dutch uses 'aan het koken zijn' for the same idea.

mistakes.wrong: Hij belde mij toen ik was aan het koken.
mistakes.right: Hij belde mij toen ik aan het koken was.
mistakes.why: The finite verb goes after the whole group 'aan het koken': 'aan het koken was'.

mistakes.wrong: Hij belde mij toen ik aan het koken.
mistakes.right: Hij belde mij toen ik aan het koken was.
mistakes.why: The toen-clause needs its finite verb 'was'; 'aan het koken' is only the progressive part.

contrast.dutch: Toen ik aan het koken was, belde hij mij.
contrast.english: While I was cooking, he phoned me.
contrast.note: Putting the toen-clause first inverts the main clause: 'belde hij mij'.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The beginning of one lesson is a single moment; 'toen' ties the seating to it.

pat-toen-10.situationNl: Het lokaal stond klaar en de docent liep naar voren. Beschrijf hoe de klas erbij zat op het begin van de cursusavond.
pat-toen-10.situationEn: Describe how the class was sitting at the very start of one evening course.

clauses.subject: de les
clauses.why: The subject 'de les' comes first and the finite verb 'begon' closes the two-word clause.

clauses.subject: iedereen
clauses.why: The finite verb 'zat' leads the main clause, then the subject 'iedereen', which takes a singular verb.

pat-toen-10.meaning: When the lesson began, everyone was in their seat.
pat-toen-10.order: 'Iedereen' is grammatically singular, so the verb is 'zat' and the possessive is 'zijn'. The place phrase closes the sentence.
pat-toen-10.forms: zitten > zat. 'Iedereen' + zijn/haar/hun: 'zijn' is the standard written choice. 'Les' is a de-word.
pat-toen-10.compare: English uses plural 'their' for 'everyone'. Dutch keeps singular 'zijn' in careful writing.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de les begon, iedereen zat op zijn plaats.
mistakes.right: Toen de les begon, zat iedereen op zijn plaats.
mistakes.why: After the comma the verb 'zat' comes first.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de les begon, zaten iedereen op zijn plaats.
mistakes.right: Toen de les begon, zat iedereen op zijn plaats.
mistakes.why: 'Iedereen' takes the singular verb 'zat'.

contrast.dutch: Iedereen zat op zijn plaats toen de les begon.
contrast.english: Everyone was in their seat when the lesson began.
contrast.note: With the main clause first the subject stays in front of the verb.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Crossing the street was one moment in which you saw her.

pat-toen-11.situationNl: Vorige week liep je door de binnenstad en zag je een bekende. Vertel wie je zag en wat je op dat moment deed.
pat-toen-11.situationEn: Say whom you saw last week and what you were doing right then in the town centre.

clauses.subject: Ik
clauses.why: Ik is first, so 'zag' is second; the pronoun 'haar' is the object. The main clause is already complete.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The object 'de straat' stands before the finite verb 'overstak', the joined past of 'oversteken'.

pat-toen-11.meaning: I saw her when I crossed the street.
pat-toen-11.order: The main clause is complete, the toen-clause adds the moment. The separable verb 'oversteken' appears joined: 'overstak'.
pat-toen-11.forms: zien > zag. oversteken > overstak (past singular). 'Straat' is a de-word.
pat-toen-11.compare: English 'crossed the street' has no particle. Dutch 'oversteken' has one and rejoins it in the toen-clause.

mistakes.wrong: Ik zag haar toen ik stak de straat over.
mistakes.right: Ik zag haar toen ik de straat overstak.
mistakes.why: In the toen-clause the separable verb is not split: 'overstak'.

mistakes.wrong: Ik zag haar toen ik de straat overstak haar.
mistakes.right: Ik zag haar toen ik de straat overstak.
mistakes.why: The object 'haar' belongs to the main clause, before the conjunction.

contrast.dutch: Toen ik de straat overstak, zag ik haar.
contrast.english: When I crossed the street, I saw her.
contrast.note: With the toen-clause first the main clause starts with 'zag ik'.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Nightfall is a single moment in the story, and the group reacted to it.

pat-toen-12.situationNl: Jullie zaten de hele middag buiten bij het meer. Het licht veranderde langzaam. Vertel wat jullie deden bij de avondschemering.
pat-toen-12.situationEn: Say what your group did as the evening light faded.

clauses.subject: het
clauses.why: The predicate 'donker' stands before the finite verb 'werd', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: we
clauses.why: The finite verb 'gingen' leads the main clause and the plural subject 'we' follows.

pat-toen-12.meaning: When it got dark, we went home.
pat-toen-12.order: 'Donker worden' uses 'worden' for a change of state, so the toen-clause ends with 'werd'. The main clause then starts with 'gingen' and ends with the direction 'naar huis'.
pat-toen-12.forms: worden > werd. gaan > ging/gingen. 'Naar huis' = to home (no article).
pat-toen-12.compare: English 'got dark' uses 'got' for the change, while Dutch uses 'werd', the past of worden, and places it behind the predicate.

mistakes.wrong: Toen het werd donker, gingen we naar huis.
mistakes.right: Toen het donker werd, gingen we naar huis.
mistakes.why: The predicate 'donker' goes before the verb 'werd'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen het donker werd, we gingen naar huis.
mistakes.right: Toen het donker werd, gingen we naar huis.
mistakes.why: The main clause needs the verb first: 'gingen we'.

contrast.dutch: We gingen naar huis toen het donker werd.
contrast.english: We went home when it got dark.
contrast.note: Main clause first: no inversion, and 'toen' still links the two moments.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Her laughter coincided with reading one piece of news.

pat-toen-13.situationNl: Een vriendin zat vorige week met haar telefoon op de bank. Opeens veranderde haar gezicht. Beschrijf haar reactie op dat moment.
pat-toen-13.situationEn: Describe a friend's reaction at the moment she read some news on her phone.

clauses.subject: Zij
clauses.why: Zij is first, so 'lachte' is second; the main clause is complete without the toen-clause.

clauses.subject: ze
clauses.why: The object 'het nieuws' stands before the finite verb 'las', which closes the clause. 'Ze' is the unstressed 'zij'.

pat-toen-13.meaning: She laughed when she read the news.
pat-toen-13.order: Two actions at the same moment: the reaction is the main clause, the trigger sits in the toen-clause. Note 'zij' and 'ze' refer to the same person.
pat-toen-13.forms: lachen > lachte. lezen > las. 'Nieuws' is a het-word and takes no plural.
pat-toen-13.compare: English 'read' is the same in past and present spelling. Dutch uses 'las' for the past.

mistakes.wrong: Zij lachte toen ze las het nieuws.
mistakes.right: Zij lachte toen ze het nieuws las.
mistakes.why: The finite verb 'las' belongs behind the object.

mistakes.wrong: Zij lachte toen ze het nieuws lezen.
mistakes.right: Zij lachte toen ze het nieuws las.
mistakes.why: The toen-clause needs a finite past form, not an infinitive.

contrast.dutch: Toen ze het nieuws las, lachte zij.
contrast.english: When she read the news, she laughed.
contrast.note: The toen-clause first makes the main clause invert: 'lachte zij'.

sense.label: toen = when (a past period)
sense.why: Childhood is a closed period in the past, so 'toen' frames where you lived.

pat-toen-14.situationNl: Een nieuwe kennis vraagt naar je afkomst. Je denkt terug aan je eerste levensjaren. Zeg in welke stad je woonde.
pat-toen-14.situationEn: Say in which city you lived in your younger years.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The predicate 'jong' stands before the finite verb 'was', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The finite verb 'woonde' leads the main clause, then 'ik' and the place 'in Gent'.

pat-toen-14.meaning: When I was young, I lived in Ghent.
pat-toen-14.order: 'Toen' covers the whole period of youth, not one instant. The main clause describes the state during that period.
pat-toen-14.forms: wonen > woonde. 'Gent' is the Dutch name of Ghent. Past of 'wonen' is regular.
pat-toen-14.compare: English 'When I was young' is identical in structure. Dutch adds the inversion in the main clause.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik jong was, ik woonde in Gent.
mistakes.right: Toen ik jong was, woonde ik in Gent.
mistakes.why: The main clause begins with the finite verb: 'woonde ik'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik was jong, woonde ik in Gent.
mistakes.right: Toen ik jong was, woonde ik in Gent.
mistakes.why: The verb 'was' belongs to the end of the toen-clause.

contrast.dutch: Als ik jong was, woonde ik in Gent.
contrast.english: If I were young, I would live in Ghent.
contrast.note: 'Als' with a past verb is ambiguous or means 'whenever'; for one past period 'toen' is the right choice.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Coming home is a single moment after work, and the tiredness belongs to it.

pat-toen-15.situationNl: Een collega had een lange dienst achter de rug. Beschrijf in welke toestand hij zijn deur binnenstapte.
pat-toen-15.situationEn: Describe the state a colleague was in at the end of a long shift.

clauses.subject: Hij
clauses.why: Hij is first, so 'was' is second; 'moe' (tired) is the predicate and completes the main clause.

clauses.subject: hij
clauses.why: The separable verb 'thuiskomen' rejoins as 'thuiskwam' at the end of the toen-clause.

pat-toen-15.meaning: He was tired when he came home.
pat-toen-15.order: The state is given first and the moment second. Both subjects are 'hij' but they sit in different clauses, and 'thuiskwam' closes the sentence.
pat-toen-15.forms: zijn > was. thuiskomen: hij kwam thuis / toen hij thuiskwam. 'Moe zijn' = to be tired.
pat-toen-15.compare: English 'came home' stays split by 'home'. Dutch glues 'thuis' to the verb in a dependent clause.

mistakes.wrong: Hij was moe toen hij kwam thuis.
mistakes.right: Hij was moe toen hij thuiskwam.
mistakes.why: Inside the toen-clause 'thuiskwam' stays whole.

mistakes.wrong: Hij moe was toen hij thuiskwam.
mistakes.right: Hij was moe toen hij thuiskwam.
mistakes.why: The main clause has the verb second: 'was moe'.

contrast.dutch: Toen hij thuiskwam, was hij moe.
contrast.english: When he came home, he was tired.
contrast.note: With the toen-clause first the main clause inverts: 'was hij'.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The train leaving is one moment, and the wave answers it.

pat-toen-16.situationNl: Op het perron nam een vriendin afscheid van je. De deuren sloten. Beschrijf wat zij deed bij het wegrijden.
pat-toen-16.situationEn: Describe what she did at the exact moment the train pulled away from the platform.

clauses.subject: de trein
clauses.why: The subject 'de trein' comes first and the finite verb 'vertrok' closes the clause.

clauses.subject: ze
clauses.why: The finite verb 'zwaaide' leads the main clause and the subject 'ze' follows.

pat-toen-16.meaning: When the train left, she waved.
pat-toen-16.order: A very short sentence with two verbs, one at the end of each clause part: 'vertrok' last in the first, 'zwaaide' first in the second.
pat-toen-16.forms: vertrekken > vertrok. zwaaien > zwaaide. 'Trein' is a de-word.
pat-toen-16.compare: English keeps 'she waved' in subject-verb order. Dutch reverses it after the opening clause.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de trein vertrok, ze zwaaide.
mistakes.right: Toen de trein vertrok, zwaaide ze.
mistakes.why: The main clause needs the finite verb first: 'zwaaide ze'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen vertrok de trein, zwaaide ze.
mistakes.right: Toen de trein vertrok, zwaaide ze.
mistakes.why: In a toen-clause the finite verb is last.

contrast.dutch: De trein vertrok en ze zwaaide.
contrast.english: The train left and she waved.
contrast.note: Two main clauses with 'en' show a sequence but not the exact trigger.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The phone call interrupted a meal at one point; 'toen' marks the moment, 'net' sharpens it.

pat-toen-17.situationNl: Het gezin zat gezellig aan tafel met een warme maaltijd. Er gebeurde iets onverwachts. Vertel wat jullie op dat moment deden.
pat-toen-17.situationEn: Tell what you were doing at the table at the moment something unexpected interrupted you.

clauses.subject: We
clauses.why: We is first, so 'aten' is second; 'net' (just) places the action right before the interruption.

clauses.subject: de telefoon
clauses.why: The subject 'de telefoon' comes first and the finite verb 'ging' closes the clause.

pat-toen-17.meaning: We were just eating when the phone rang.
pat-toen-17.order: 'Net' (just) is placed after the verb in the main clause and sharpens the moment. The toen-clause names the interruption and is short.
pat-toen-17.forms: eten > at/aten. gaan > ging (here: to ring). 'Telefoon' is a de-word.
pat-toen-17.compare: English uses 'were just eating' (continuous). Dutch uses the simple past with 'net'.

mistakes.wrong: We net aten toen de telefoon ging.
mistakes.right: We aten net toen de telefoon ging.
mistakes.why: The main clause has the verb second: 'aten net'.

mistakes.wrong: We aten net toen ging de telefoon.
mistakes.right: We aten net toen de telefoon ging.
mistakes.why: The toen-clause needs the verb at the end: 'de telefoon ging'.

contrast.dutch: Net toen de telefoon ging, aten we.
contrast.english: Just when the phone rang, we were eating.
contrast.note: 'Net toen' can open the sentence; the main clause then inverts to 'aten we'.

sense.label: toen = when (a past period)
sense.why: Childhood is a closed period; 'toen' sets the frame for what you did then.

pat-toen-18.situationNl: Een jonge collega vraagt hoe jouw jeugd eruitzag. Je denkt terug aan de straat waar je opgroeide. Vertel waar je speelde.
pat-toen-18.situationEn: Say where you played during your early years, using the period of being a small child.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The predicate 'klein' stands before the finite verb 'was', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The finite verb 'speelde' leads the main clause, then 'ik' and 'buiten'.

pat-toen-18.meaning: When I was little, I played outside.
pat-toen-18.order: A period, not an instant: the main clause tells what usually happened in that period. 'Toen' introduces the period; 'als' would be needed only for a single repeated trigger.
pat-toen-18.forms: spelen > speelde. 'Klein zijn' = to be small/little. 'Buiten' = outside (adverb).
pat-toen-18.compare: English 'When I was little' is the same. The Dutch main clause inverts and has 'buiten' at the end.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik klein was, ik speelde buiten.
mistakes.right: Toen ik klein was, speelde ik buiten.
mistakes.why: After the comma the main clause starts with its verb.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik was klein, speelde ik buiten.
mistakes.right: Toen ik klein was, speelde ik buiten.
mistakes.why: The finite verb 'was' goes behind 'klein'.

contrast.dutch: Vroeger speelde ik buiten.
contrast.english: In the past I played outside.
contrast.note: 'Vroeger' (formerly) gives the period as an adverb, so no subordinate clause is needed.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The loss of the bag happened at the moment of getting off, so 'toen' fits.

pat-toen-19.situationNl: Een vriendin kwam gisteren aan op haar bestemming en liep zonder haar bagage naar de uitgang. Vertel hoe dat gebeurde.
pat-toen-19.situationEn: Explain how a friend lost her bag at the moment she left a train.

clauses.subject: Zij
clauses.why: Zij is first, so 'vergat' is second; 'haar tas' is the object.

clauses.subject: ze
clauses.why: The separable verb 'uitstappen' rejoins as 'uitstapte' at the end of the clause.

pat-toen-19.meaning: She forgot her bag when she got off.
pat-toen-19.order: The main clause tells what went wrong, the toen-clause when. Because the whole story is in the past, both verbs are past tense.
pat-toen-19.forms: vergeten > vergat. uitstappen: ze stapt uit / toen ze uitstapte. 'Tas' is a de-word.
pat-toen-19.compare: English 'got off' is a phrasal verb. Dutch 'uitstappen' is a separable verb that rejoins in the dependent clause.

mistakes.wrong: Zij vergat haar tas toen ze stapte uit.
mistakes.right: Zij vergat haar tas toen ze uitstapte.
mistakes.why: The separable verb stays whole: 'uitstapte'.

mistakes.wrong: Zij vergat toen ze uitstapte haar tas.
mistakes.right: Zij vergat haar tas toen ze uitstapte.
mistakes.why: The object 'haar tas' belongs to the main clause, before the conjunction.

contrast.dutch: Toen ze uitstapte, vergat zij haar tas.
contrast.english: When she got off, she forgot her bag.
contrast.note: The toen-clause first inverts the main clause: 'vergat zij'.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The first drops are one moment; the run indoors is the reaction.

pat-toen-20.situationNl: Jullie zaten midden in een wandeling door het park. De lucht werd donker. Vertel wat jullie deden bij de eerste druppels.
pat-toen-20.situationEn: Say what your group did at the very first drops of rain during a walk.

clauses.subject: het
clauses.why: The finite verb 'begon' leads the verb group 'begon te regenen' and the clause ends with the infinitive 'regenen'.

clauses.subject: we
clauses.why: The finite verb 'renden' leads the main clause, then 'we' and 'naar binnen'.

pat-toen-20.meaning: When it began to rain, we ran inside.
pat-toen-20.order: 'Beginnen te' + infinitive describes the start of an event. The finite verb 'begon' is not the last word of the toen-clause: 'te regenen' follows it.
pat-toen-20.forms: beginnen te regenen: te + infinitive. rennen > rende/renden. 'Naar binnen' = inside (direction).
pat-toen-20.compare: English 'began to rain' has the same pattern. Dutch adds 'te' before the infinitive in the same way.

mistakes.wrong: Toen het begon regenen, renden we naar binnen.
mistakes.right: Toen het begon te regenen, renden we naar binnen.
mistakes.why: With 'beginnen' the infinitive needs 'te': 'te regenen'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen het begon te regenen, we renden naar binnen.
mistakes.right: Toen het begon te regenen, renden we naar binnen.
mistakes.why: The main clause needs the verb first: 'renden we'.

contrast.dutch: We renden naar binnen toen het begon te regenen.
contrast.english: We ran inside when it began to rain.
contrast.note: Main clause first: normal word order and the toen-clause closes the sentence.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The outage began at one moment, and the call was the reaction.

clauses.subject: de storing
clauses.why: The subject 'de storing' comes first and the finite verb 'begon' closes the clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: After the toen-clause the finite verb 'belde' comes first, then 'ik' and the object 'de helpdesk'.

pat-toen-21.meaning: When the outage started, I called the helpdesk.
pat-toen-21.order: The cause is the start of the outage, the reaction is the call. The comma divides the two verb positions: 'begon' last, 'belde' first.
pat-toen-21.forms: beginnen > begon. bellen > belde. 'De helpdesk' is a de-word and the direct object of 'belde'.
pat-toen-21.compare: English 'called the helpdesk' needs no preposition; neither does Dutch 'bellen' with a direct object.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de storing begon, ik belde de helpdesk.
mistakes.right: Toen de storing begon, belde ik de helpdesk.
mistakes.why: After an opening toen-clause the main verb comes first: 'belde ik'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen begon de storing, belde ik de helpdesk.
mistakes.right: Toen de storing begon, belde ik de helpdesk.
mistakes.why: In the toen-clause the finite verb is last: 'de storing begon'.

contrast.dutch: Ik belde de helpdesk toen de storing begon.
contrast.english: I called the helpdesk when the outage started.
contrast.note: With the main clause first the subject stays before the verb.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Reading the email was one act in the past; the understanding followed from it.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The object 'de e-mail' stands before the finite verb 'las', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The finite verb 'begreep' comes first after the comma, then 'ik' and the object 'het probleem'.

pat-toen-22.meaning: When I read the email, I understood the problem.
pat-toen-22.order: Understanding came out of reading, so the toen-clause comes first as the background. The object 'de e-mail' precedes 'las'.
pat-toen-22.forms: lezen > las. begrijpen > begreep. 'E-mail' is a de-word here, 'probleem' a het-word.
pat-toen-22.compare: English 'read' is the same in the past. Dutch uses the different form 'las' and moves it behind the object.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik las de e-mail, begreep ik het probleem.
mistakes.right: Toen ik de e-mail las, begreep ik het probleem.
mistakes.why: The finite verb 'las' goes to the end of the toen-clause.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik de e-mail las, ik begreep het probleem.
mistakes.right: Toen ik de e-mail las, begreep ik het probleem.
mistakes.why: The main clause starts with its verb: 'begreep ik'.

contrast.dutch: Na het lezen van de e-mail begreep ik het probleem.
contrast.english: After reading the email, I understood the problem.
contrast.note: A prepositional phrase with a noun replaces the clause.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The customer entering was a single moment that you were ready for.

clauses.subject: de klant
clauses.why: The separable verb 'binnenkomen' rejoins at the end of the clause as 'binnenkwam'.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The finite verb 'stond' leads the main clause, then 'ik', the adverb 'al' and the particle 'klaar'.

pat-toen-23.meaning: When the customer came in, I was already ready.
pat-toen-23.order: The toen-clause is only subject and joined verb. The main clause then reads verb, subject, 'al', 'klaar': the readiness is stated as a posture, 'stond klaar'.
pat-toen-23.forms: binnenkomen: komt binnen / toen hij binnenkwam. staan > stond. 'Klant' is a de-word.
pat-toen-23.compare: English 'came in' is a phrasal verb. Dutch 'binnenkomen' is a separable verb that rejoins in the dependent clause.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de klant kwam binnen, stond ik al klaar.
mistakes.right: Toen de klant binnenkwam, stond ik al klaar.
mistakes.why: The separable verb stays whole in the toen-clause.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de klant binnenkwam, ik stond al klaar.
mistakes.right: Toen de klant binnenkwam, stond ik al klaar.
mistakes.why: After the comma the verb comes first: 'stond ik'.

contrast.dutch: De klant kwam binnen en ik stond al klaar.
contrast.english: The customer came in and I was already ready.
contrast.note: With 'en' both clauses are main clauses with the verb second.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The restart is one event, and the warning was its direct consequence.

clauses.subject: het systeem
clauses.why: The adverb 'opnieuw' stands between the subject and the finite verb 'startte', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: een waarschuwing
clauses.why: The finite verb 'verscheen' comes first, then the placeholder 'er' and the new subject 'een waarschuwing'.

pat-toen-24.meaning: When the system restarted, a warning appeared.
pat-toen-24.order: 'Opnieuw' (again) sits before the finite verb in the toen-clause. 'Er' introduces the indefinite subject after the verb.
pat-toen-24.forms: starten > startte. verschijnen > verscheen. 'Systeem' is a het-word; 'waarschuwing' a de-word.
pat-toen-24.compare: English 'a warning appeared' keeps subject-first. Dutch typically adds 'er' to introduce a new subject after the verb.

mistakes.wrong: Toen het systeem startte opnieuw, verscheen er een waarschuwing.
mistakes.right: Toen het systeem opnieuw startte, verscheen er een waarschuwing.
mistakes.why: The adverb 'opnieuw' goes before the verb 'startte' at the end.

mistakes.wrong: Toen het systeem opnieuw startte, een waarschuwing verscheen.
mistakes.right: Toen het systeem opnieuw startte, verscheen er een waarschuwing.
mistakes.why: The main clause needs the verb first: 'verscheen er een waarschuwing'.

contrast.dutch: Er verscheen een waarschuwing toen het systeem opnieuw startte.
contrast.english: A warning appeared when the system restarted.
contrast.note: Main clause first: 'er' stays at the beginning.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The entry of the password was a single act with a single outcome.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The separable verb 'invoeren' rejoins as 'invoerde' at the end of the clause, behind the object 'het wachtwoord'.

clauses.subject: het
clauses.why: The finite verb 'werd' comes first after the comma, then 'het' and the participle 'geweigerd' as a passive.

pat-toen-25.meaning: When I entered the password, it was rejected.
pat-toen-25.order: The toen-clause ends in the joined verb 'invoerde'. The main clause is a passive, so the participle 'geweigerd' stands at the very end and 'werd' leads it.
pat-toen-25.forms: invoeren: voert in / toen ik invoerde. weigeren > geweigerd. 'Wachtwoord' is a het-word.
pat-toen-25.compare: English 'was rejected' is a passive too. Dutch passive 'werd geweigerd' puts the participle at the end of the clause.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik voerde het wachtwoord in, werd het geweigerd.
mistakes.right: Toen ik het wachtwoord invoerde, werd het geweigerd.
mistakes.why: In the toen-clause the separable verb stays in one piece.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik het wachtwoord invoerde, het werd geweigerd.
mistakes.right: Toen ik het wachtwoord invoerde, werd het geweigerd.
mistakes.why: The main clause starts with its verb: 'werd het geweigerd'.

contrast.dutch: Mijn wachtwoord werd geweigerd bij het invoeren.
contrast.english: My password was rejected on entering.
contrast.note: A shorter version with a noun phrase and no toen-clause.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The colleague's departure is a single past moment.

clauses.subject: mijn collega
clauses.why: The subject 'mijn collega' comes first and the finite verb 'vertrok' closes the clause.

clauses.subject: hij
clauses.why: The finite verb 'nam' comes first, then 'hij' and the object; the particle 'mee' at the end completes 'meenemen'.

pat-toen-26.meaning: When my colleague left, he took the key with him.
pat-toen-26.order: The separable verb 'meenemen' splits in the main clause: 'nam ... mee'. The particle goes to the end, behind the object.
pat-toen-26.forms: meenemen: neemt mee / nam mee. vertrekken > vertrok. 'Sleutel' is a de-word.
pat-toen-26.compare: English 'took with him' keeps 'with' near the object. Dutch 'mee' is the final particle of 'meenemen'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen mijn collega vertrok, nam mee hij de sleutel.
mistakes.right: Toen mijn collega vertrok, nam hij de sleutel mee.
mistakes.why: The particle 'mee' belongs at the end of the main clause.

mistakes.wrong: Toen mijn collega vertrok, hij nam de sleutel mee.
mistakes.right: Toen mijn collega vertrok, nam hij de sleutel mee.
mistakes.why: After the comma the verb comes first: 'nam hij'.

contrast.dutch: Mijn collega nam de sleutel mee toen hij vertrok.
contrast.english: My colleague took the key with him when he left.
contrast.note: Main clause first, so the subject is at the front; the verb still splits.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Leaving the office is a single moment for which you recall the weather.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The object 'het kantoor' stands before the finite verb 'verliet', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: het
clauses.why: The finite verb 'regende' leads the main clause, then 'het' and the phrase 'nog steeds'.

pat-toen-27.meaning: When I left the office, it was still raining.
pat-toen-27.order: The object 'het kantoor' separates subject and verb in the toen-clause. In the main clause the weather verb comes first, then 'het', then the closing 'nog steeds'.
pat-toen-27.forms: verlaten > verliet (strong verb with inseparable ver-). regenen > regende. 'Kantoor' is a het-word.
pat-toen-27.compare: English 'left' is the same in past and present spelling for a different verb; Dutch has a separate past form 'verliet'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik verliet het kantoor, regende het nog steeds.
mistakes.right: Toen ik het kantoor verliet, regende het nog steeds.
mistakes.why: The finite verb 'verliet' belongs behind its object.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik het kantoor verliet, het regende nog steeds.
mistakes.right: Toen ik het kantoor verliet, regende het nog steeds.
mistakes.why: After the comma 'regende het' needs the verb first.

contrast.dutch: Het regende nog steeds toen ik het kantoor verliet.
contrast.english: It was still raining when I left the office.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, the weather leads and 'verliet' ends the sentence in the toen-clause.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The lift stopping is one event with an immediate consequence.

clauses.subject: de lift
clauses.why: The subject 'de lift' comes first and the finite verb 'stopte' closes the clause.

clauses.subject: we
clauses.why: The finite verb 'zaten' comes first after the comma, then the plural subject 'we' and the particle 'vast'.

pat-toen-28.meaning: When the lift stopped, we were stuck.
pat-toen-28.order: Both clauses are very short. After the comma the verb 'zaten' leads and the particle 'vast' ends the sentence, so the sense of being trapped lands on the last word.
pat-toen-28.forms: stoppen > stopte. vastzitten > zat vast / zaten vast. 'Lift' is a de-word.
pat-toen-28.compare: English 'were stuck' is a passive-like state. Dutch 'zaten vast' uses the verb 'zitten'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de lift stopte, we zaten vast.
mistakes.right: Toen de lift stopte, zaten we vast.
mistakes.why: The main clause begins with its verb: 'zaten we'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de lift stopte, zaten vast we.
mistakes.right: Toen de lift stopte, zaten we vast.
mistakes.why: The particle 'vast' comes after the subject: 'zaten we vast'.

contrast.dutch: De lift stopte en we zaten vast.
contrast.english: The lift stopped and we were stuck.
contrast.note: With 'en' the two events are listed in order without a causal frame.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Finishing the test is one moment after which you sent the results.

clauses.text: Toen ik klaar was met de test
clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The predicate 'klaar' stands before the finite verb 'was'; the phrase 'met de test' trails behind it.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The finite verb 'stuurde' comes first, then 'ik', the object and the particle 'op', which completes 'opsturen'.

pat-toen-29.meaning: When I was finished with the test, I sent in the results.
pat-toen-29.order: 'Klaar zijn met' (to be done with) takes a phrase that may follow the verb. The separable verb 'opsturen' splits in the main clause.
pat-toen-29.forms: opsturen: stuurt op / stuurde op. 'Klaar zijn met iets' = to be finished with something.
pat-toen-29.compare: English 'sent in' is a phrasal verb with a movable particle. Dutch 'opsturen' puts 'op' at the end.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik klaar was met de test, ik stuurde de resultaten op.
mistakes.right: Toen ik klaar was met de test, stuurde ik de resultaten op.
mistakes.why: After the comma the verb comes first: 'stuurde ik'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik klaar was met de test, stuurde ik op de resultaten.
mistakes.right: Toen ik klaar was met de test, stuurde ik de resultaten op.
mistakes.why: The particle 'op' goes behind the object.

contrast.dutch: Na de test stuurde ik de resultaten op.
contrast.english: After the test I sent in the results.
contrast.note: A noun phrase 'na de test' replaces the whole toen-clause, so the verb stays second.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The boss's call is a single moment against which you say where you were.

clauses.subject: de baas
clauses.why: The subject 'de baas' comes first and the finite verb 'belde' closes the clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The finite verb 'zat' comes first, then 'ik' and the place phrase 'in de trein'.

pat-toen-30.meaning: When the boss called, I was on the train.
pat-toen-30.order: The toen-clause only names the caller and the call. The main clause locates you: the verb 'zat' first, then 'ik', then the place phrase 'in de trein'.
pat-toen-30.forms: bellen > belde. zitten > zat. 'In de trein' = on the train (Dutch uses 'in').
pat-toen-30.compare: English says 'on the train'. Dutch uses 'in de trein' and the verb 'zitten' for being seated.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de baas belde, ik zat in de trein.
mistakes.right: Toen de baas belde, zat ik in de trein.
mistakes.why: The main clause starts with the verb: 'zat ik'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de baas belde, zat ik op de trein.
mistakes.right: Toen de baas belde, zat ik in de trein.
mistakes.why: Dutch uses 'in de trein', not 'op de trein'.

contrast.dutch: Ik zat in de trein toen de baas belde.
contrast.english: I was on the train when the boss called.
contrast.note: The main clause first keeps the subject in front.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Opening the door is a single moment at which the smell struck you.

clauses.subject: we
clauses.why: The object 'de deur' stands before the finite verb 'openden', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: het
clauses.why: The finite verb 'rook' comes first, then 'het' and the phrase 'naar koffie'.

pat-toen-31.meaning: When we opened the door, it smelled of coffee.
pat-toen-31.order: The sensory verb 'rook' leads the main clause after the comma, followed by the dummy subject 'het'. The source of the smell is added with 'naar koffie'.
pat-toen-31.forms: openen > opende/openden. ruiken > rook. 'Koffie' needs no article.
pat-toen-31.compare: English 'smelled of coffee' is close, but Dutch needs 'naar' and the dummy 'het' after the verb. Try describing smells this way.

mistakes.wrong: Toen we openden de deur, rook het naar koffie.
mistakes.right: Toen we de deur openden, rook het naar koffie.
mistakes.why: The object goes before the verb 'openden'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen we de deur openden, rook het van koffie.
mistakes.right: Toen we de deur openden, rook het naar koffie.
mistakes.why: Dutch 'ruiken' takes the preposition 'naar' for the smell source; 'van' is not used here.

contrast.dutch: Het rook naar koffie toen we de deur openden.
contrast.english: It smelled of coffee when we opened the door.
contrast.note: With the main clause first the dummy 'het' leads and the toen-clause ends the sentence with 'openden'.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Hearing the news was a single moment and your disbelief followed at once.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The object 'het nieuws' stands before the finite verb 'hoorde', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The modal 'kon' comes first, then 'ik', the object 'het', the negation 'niet' and the infinitive 'geloven'.

pat-toen-32.meaning: When I heard the news, I could not believe it.
pat-toen-32.order: Hearing is the trigger; disbelief is the reaction. After the comma the modal 'kon' leads, 'het niet' sits before the closing infinitive 'geloven'.
pat-toen-32.forms: horen > hoorde. kunnen > kon. geloven: infinitive after the modal.
pat-toen-32.compare: English 'could not believe it' keeps 'it' after the verb. Dutch places the object 'het' before 'niet geloven'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik het nieuws hoorde, ik kon het niet geloven.
mistakes.right: Toen ik het nieuws hoorde, kon ik het niet geloven.
mistakes.why: The modal comes first after the comma: 'kon ik'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik het nieuws hoorde, kon ik geloven het niet.
mistakes.right: Toen ik het nieuws hoorde, kon ik het niet geloven.
mistakes.why: The object 'het' and 'niet' go before the infinitive 'geloven'.

contrast.dutch: Ik kon het niet geloven toen ik het nieuws hoorde.
contrast.english: I could not believe it when I heard the news.
contrast.note: With the main clause first the modal chain stays together: 'kon ... geloven', and the toen-clause adds the moment at the end.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The end of the lesson is a single moment after which the group went to lunch.

clauses.subject: de les
clauses.why: The participle 'afgelopen' used as a predicate stands before the finite verb 'was', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: we
clauses.why: The finite verb 'gingen' comes first, then 'we', the adverb 'samen' and the infinitive 'lunchen'.

pat-toen-33.meaning: When the lesson was over, we went to lunch together.
pat-toen-33.order: The state 'afgelopen was' ends the toen-clause. The main clause then lists a motion verb and an infinitive: 'gingen we samen lunchen'.
pat-toen-33.forms: aflopen > afgelopen. gaan lunchen: finite 'gingen' plus infinitive. 'Samen' = together.
pat-toen-33.compare: English 'went to lunch' uses a noun. Dutch uses the infinitive 'lunchen' after 'gaan'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de les was afgelopen, gingen we samen lunchen.
mistakes.right: Toen de les afgelopen was, gingen we samen lunchen.
mistakes.why: The participle comes before the verb: 'afgelopen was'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de les afgelopen was, we gingen samen lunchen.
mistakes.right: Toen de les afgelopen was, gingen we samen lunchen.
mistakes.why: With 'gaan lunchen' the subject 'we' must follow the verb 'gingen' once the toen-clause has opened the sentence.

contrast.dutch: We gingen samen lunchen toen de les afgelopen was.
contrast.english: We went to lunch together when the lesson was over.
contrast.note: Starting with the main clause removes the inversion: 'we gingen samen lunchen', and the toen-clause closes with 'afgelopen was'.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Searching for the bag is one moment in which the pass turned up.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The object 'mijn tas' stands before the finite verb 'zocht', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The finite verb 'vond' leads the main clause, then 'ik' and the object 'mijn oude pas'.

pat-toen-34.meaning: When I looked for my bag, I found my old pass.
pat-toen-34.order: Two past verbs in a row: 'zocht' ends the first part, 'vond' starts the second. The searching and the finding are joined by the same moment.
pat-toen-34.forms: zoeken > zocht. vinden > vond. 'Mijn oude pas': 'oud' takes -e after a possessive.
pat-toen-34.compare: English uses 'looked for'. Dutch uses the single verb 'zoeken' without a preposition.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik zocht mijn tas, vond ik mijn oude pas.
mistakes.right: Toen ik mijn tas zocht, vond ik mijn oude pas.
mistakes.why: The finite verb belongs behind the object.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik mijn tas zocht, vond ik mijn oud pas.
mistakes.right: Toen ik mijn tas zocht, vond ik mijn oude pas.
mistakes.why: After a possessive the adjective takes -e: 'mijn oude pas'.

contrast.dutch: Ik vond mijn oude pas toen ik mijn tas zocht.
contrast.english: I found my old pass when I looked for my bag.
contrast.note: With the main clause first the finding leads: 'ik vond mijn oude pas', then the toen-clause names the search.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The alarm sounding is one event, and the evacuation followed it.

clauses.subject: het alarm
clauses.why: The separable verb 'afgaan' rejoins as 'afging' at the end of the clause.

clauses.subject: iedereen
clauses.why: The finite verb 'liep' comes first, then the singular 'iedereen' and the direction 'naar buiten'.

pat-toen-35.meaning: When the alarm went off, everyone walked outside.
pat-toen-35.order: The alarm clause ends in the joined verb 'afging'. The main clause starts with 'liep' and gives a direction phrase 'naar buiten' that ends the sentence.
pat-toen-35.forms: afgaan: gaat af / ging af / toen het afging. lopen > liep. 'Alarm' is a het-word.
pat-toen-35.compare: English 'went off' is a phrasal verb; Dutch 'afgaan' is a separable verb that rejoins in the dependent clause.

mistakes.wrong: Toen het alarm ging af, liep iedereen naar buiten.
mistakes.right: Toen het alarm afging, liep iedereen naar buiten.
mistakes.why: The verb 'afgaan' is written together in a dependent clause: 'afging', not 'ging af'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen het alarm afging, iedereen liep naar buiten.
mistakes.right: Toen het alarm afging, liep iedereen naar buiten.
mistakes.why: After the comma the main clause begins with the verb.

contrast.dutch: Iedereen liep naar buiten toen het alarm afging.
contrast.english: Everyone walked outside when the alarm went off.
contrast.note: With the main clause first the subject 'iedereen' leads and the toen-clause closes with 'afging'.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Coming back is a single moment; the meeting was already over by then.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The separable verb 'terugkomen' rejoins as 'terugkwam' at the end of the two-word clause.

clauses.subject: de vergadering
clauses.why: The finite verb 'was' leads the main clause, then 'de vergadering', the adverb 'al' and the predicate 'voorbij'.

pat-toen-36.meaning: When I came back, the meeting was already over.
pat-toen-36.order: The return is expressed with a joined verb 'terugkwam'. In the main clause the verb 'was' leads, then the subject, then 'al voorbij', which stresses that the meeting had ended earlier.
pat-toen-36.forms: terugkomen: komt terug / kwam terug / toen ik terugkwam. 'Vergadering' is a de-word.
pat-toen-36.compare: English 'came back' is a phrasal verb. Dutch glues the particle on in the dependent clause.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik kwam terug, was de vergadering al voorbij.
mistakes.right: Toen ik terugkwam, was de vergadering al voorbij.
mistakes.why: The verb 'terugkomen' is written together in a dependent clause: 'terugkwam'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik terugkwam, de vergadering was al voorbij.
mistakes.right: Toen ik terugkwam, was de vergadering al voorbij.
mistakes.why: The main clause after the comma opens with 'was', the verb that links the meeting to 'al voorbij'.

contrast.dutch: De vergadering was al voorbij toen ik terugkwam.
contrast.english: The meeting was already over when I came back.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, 'de vergadering' leads and the toen-clause ends the sentence with 'terugkwam'.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The internet failing is one moment after which work continued offline.

clauses.subject: het internet
clauses.why: The separable verb 'uitvallen' rejoins as 'uitviel' at the end of the clause.

clauses.subject: we
clauses.why: The finite verb 'werkten' comes first, then 'we', 'offline' and the particle 'verder', which completes 'verderwerken'.

pat-toen-37.meaning: When the internet went down, we carried on working offline.
pat-toen-37.order: The failure clause ends in the joined verb 'uitviel'. The main clause splits its own separable verb: 'werkten' second after the inversion, the particle 'verder' last.
pat-toen-37.forms: uitvallen > viel uit / uitviel. verderwerken > werkte verder. 'Internet' is a het-word.
pat-toen-37.compare: English 'carried on working' is a verb chain. Dutch uses the single separable verb 'verderwerken'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen het internet viel uit, werkten we offline verder.
mistakes.right: Toen het internet uitviel, werkten we offline verder.
mistakes.why: The verb 'uitvallen' is written together in a dependent clause: 'uitviel', not 'viel uit'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen het internet uitviel, werkten verder we offline.
mistakes.right: Toen het internet uitviel, werkten we offline verder.
mistakes.why: The particle 'verder' goes after the subject and 'offline'.

contrast.dutch: We werkten offline verder toen het internet uitviel.
contrast.english: We carried on working offline when the internet went down.
contrast.note: With the main clause first the subject 'we' leads, 'werkten' follows, and 'uitviel' ends the sentence.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The start of the new colleague is one moment at which he received a tour.

clauses.subject: de nieuwe collega
clauses.why: The subject 'de nieuwe collega' comes first and the finite verb 'begon' closes the clause.

clauses.subject: hij
clauses.why: The finite verb 'kreeg' leads the main clause, then 'hij' and the object 'een rondleiding'.

pat-toen-38.meaning: When the new colleague started, he got a tour.
pat-toen-38.order: The toen-clause is subject and verb only. The main clause starts with the verb 'kreeg', then 'hij', then the object 'een rondleiding'.
pat-toen-38.forms: beginnen > begon. krijgen > kreeg. 'Nieuwe collega': 'nieuw' takes -e after the definite article.
pat-toen-38.compare: English 'got a tour' uses the same simple past. Dutch 'kreeg hij' inverts after the opening clause.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de nieuwe collega begon, hij kreeg een rondleiding.
mistakes.right: Toen de nieuwe collega begon, kreeg hij een rondleiding.
mistakes.why: After the comma the main clause opens with 'kreeg', not with the subject 'hij'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de nieuwe collega begon, kreeg hij een rondleidingen.
mistakes.right: Toen de nieuwe collega begon, kreeg hij een rondleiding.
mistakes.why: 'Rondleiding' is singular after 'een'; an -en plural would not match the article here.

contrast.dutch: De nieuwe collega kreeg een rondleiding toen hij begon.
contrast.english: The new colleague got a tour when he started.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, 'de nieuwe collega' leads and the toen-clause adds when it happened.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Seeing the error is a single moment; your warning came right away.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The object 'de fout' stands before the finite verb 'zag', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The finite verb 'waarschuwde' leads, then 'ik', the adverb 'meteen' and the object 'mijn team'.

pat-toen-39.meaning: When I saw the error, I warned my team immediately.
pat-toen-39.order: 'Meteen' sits between the subject and the object in the main clause. The toen-clause stays short: the object 'de fout' and the verb 'zag'.
pat-toen-39.forms: zien > zag. waarschuwen > waarschuwde. 'Team' is a het-word.
pat-toen-39.compare: English 'warned my team immediately' ends with the adverb. Dutch usually puts 'meteen' before the object.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik de fout zag, ik waarschuwde meteen mijn team.
mistakes.right: Toen ik de fout zag, waarschuwde ik meteen mijn team.
mistakes.why: After the comma the main clause opens with 'waarschuwde', not with the subject 'ik'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik de fout zag, waarschuwde ik meteen team mijn.
mistakes.right: Toen ik de fout zag, waarschuwde ik meteen mijn team.
mistakes.why: The possessive 'mijn' stands before its noun: 'mijn team', never after it.

contrast.dutch: Ik waarschuwde meteen mijn team toen ik de fout zag.
contrast.english: I warned my team immediately when I saw the error.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, 'ik waarschuwde meteen mijn team' leads and 'zag' ends the sentence.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The children falling asleep is one moment that allowed the tidying.

clauses.subject: de kinderen
clauses.why: The plural subject 'de kinderen' comes first and the plural finite verb 'sliepen' closes the clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The finite verb 'ruimde' leads the main clause, then 'ik', the object and the particle 'op' of 'opruimen'.

pat-toen-40.meaning: When the children were asleep, I tidied up the kitchen.
pat-toen-40.order: The sleeping clause ends in the plural verb 'sliepen'. The main clause starts with 'ruimde', and the particle 'op' ends it after the object.
pat-toen-40.forms: slapen > sliep / sliepen. opruimen > ruimde op. 'Keuken' is a de-word.
pat-toen-40.compare: English 'tidied up' keeps the particle next to the verb. Dutch puts 'op' after the object.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de kinderen sliepen, ik ruimde de keuken op.
mistakes.right: Toen de kinderen sliepen, ruimde ik de keuken op.
mistakes.why: After the comma the main clause opens with 'ruimde', not with the subject 'ik'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de kinderen sliepen, ruimde ik op de keuken.
mistakes.right: Toen de kinderen sliepen, ruimde ik de keuken op.
mistakes.why: The object 'de keuken' goes before the particle: 'ruimde ik de keuken op', not with 'op' in front of the object.

contrast.dutch: Ik ruimde de keuken op toen de kinderen sliepen.
contrast.english: I tidied the kitchen when the children were asleep.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, 'ik ruimde de keuken op' leads and 'sliepen' closes the sentence.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The power failing interrupted work at one moment; 'net' sharpens how close the two were.

clauses.text: Ik was net aan het werk
clauses.subject: Ik
clauses.why: Ik is first, so 'was' is second; 'net aan het werk' (just at work) finishes the progressive frame.

clauses.subject: de stroom
clauses.why: The subject 'de stroom' comes first and the joined separable verb 'uitviel' closes the clause.

pat-toen-41.meaning: I had just started working when the power failed.
pat-toen-41.order: The main clause sets the activity, the toen-clause cuts into it. Because the main clause opens, the subject stays first and no inversion occurs.
pat-toen-41.forms: uitvallen: de stroom valt uit / viel uit / toen de stroom uitviel. 'Aan het werk zijn' = to be at work. 'Stroom' is a de-word.
pat-toen-41.compare: English 'had just started working' uses a perfect. Dutch uses the simple past 'was net aan het werk'.

mistakes.wrong: Ik was net aan het werk toen de stroom viel uit.
mistakes.right: Ik was net aan het werk toen de stroom uitviel.
mistakes.why: The verb 'uitvallen' is written together at the end of the toen-clause: 'uitviel'.

mistakes.wrong: Ik net was aan het werk toen de stroom uitviel.
mistakes.right: Ik was net aan het werk toen de stroom uitviel.
mistakes.why: 'Net' follows the finite verb in the main clause: 'was net'.

contrast.dutch: Toen de stroom uitviel, was ik net aan het werk.
contrast.english: When the power failed, I was just at work.
contrast.note: Moving the toen-clause first makes the main clause invert to 'was ik'.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The crying was triggered at the moment of hearing the news.

clauses.subject: Ze
clauses.why: Ze is first, so 'huilde' is second; the clause is complete without the rest.

clauses.text: toen ze het slechte nieuws hoorde
clauses.subject: ze
clauses.why: The object 'het slechte nieuws' stands before the finite verb 'hoorde', which closes the clause.

pat-toen-42.meaning: She cried when she heard the bad news.
pat-toen-42.order: A one-word reaction with a longer trigger. The adjective 'slechte' takes -e because 'nieuws' follows 'het' and is a het-word with a definite article.
pat-toen-42.forms: huilen > huilde. horen > hoorde. 'Het slechte nieuws': definite article plus -e.
pat-toen-42.compare: English 'the bad news' has no ending on the adjective; Dutch needs -e after 'het' here.

mistakes.wrong: Ze huilde toen ze hoorde het slechte nieuws.
mistakes.right: Ze huilde toen ze het slechte nieuws hoorde.
mistakes.why: The object goes before the verb 'hoorde' at the end of the toen-clause.

mistakes.wrong: Ze huilde toen ze het slecht nieuws hoorde.
mistakes.right: Ze huilde toen ze het slechte nieuws hoorde.
mistakes.why: After the definite article 'het' the adjective needs -e: 'slechte'.

contrast.dutch: Bij het slechte nieuws huilde ze.
contrast.english: At the bad news she cried.
contrast.note: A prepositional phrase replaces the toen-clause; the verb stays second.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The crash coincided with the installation.

clauses.subject: De server
clauses.why: 'De server' is first, so the finite verb 'crashte' is second; the clause is complete.

clauses.subject: wij
clauses.why: The object 'de update' stands before the plural finite verb 'installeerden', which closes the clause.

pat-toen-43.meaning: The server crashed when we installed the update.
pat-toen-43.order: The consequence is placed first and the trigger second. Both verbs are weak past forms: 'crashte' ends in -te, 'installeerden' (plural) in -den.
pat-toen-43.forms: crashen > crashte. installeren > installeerde / installeerden (plural). 'Update' is a de-word.
pat-toen-43.compare: English 'installed' is the same for singular and plural. Dutch has 'installeerde' and 'installeerden'.

mistakes.wrong: De server crashte toen wij de update installeerde.
mistakes.right: De server crashte toen wij de update installeerden.
mistakes.why: Plural 'wij' needs the plural past 'installeerden'.

mistakes.wrong: De server crashte toen wij installeerden de update.
mistakes.right: De server crashte toen wij de update installeerden.
mistakes.why: The object goes before the verb in the toen-clause.

contrast.dutch: Toen wij de update installeerden, crashte de server.
contrast.english: When we installed the update, the server crashed.
contrast.note: Toen-clause first: the main clause inverts to 'crashte de server'.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Your train leaving is the moment against which you describe where you stood.

clauses.subject: Ik
clauses.why: Ik is first, so 'stond' is second; 'op het perron' is the place phrase.

clauses.subject: mijn trein
clauses.why: The subject 'mijn trein' comes first and the finite verb 'vertrok' closes the clause.

pat-toen-44.meaning: I was standing on the platform when my train left.
pat-toen-44.order: 'Staan' is used for being upright on a platform. The place phrase belongs to the main clause, not to the toen-clause.
pat-toen-44.forms: staan > stond. vertrekken > vertrok. 'Perron' is a het-word.
pat-toen-44.compare: English 'was standing' is a continuous. Dutch uses the plain past 'stond'.

mistakes.wrong: Ik stond op het perron toen vertrok mijn trein.
mistakes.right: Ik stond op het perron toen mijn trein vertrok.
mistakes.why: In the toen-clause the verb is last: 'mijn trein vertrok'.

mistakes.wrong: Ik was op het perron staan toen mijn trein vertrok.
mistakes.right: Ik stond op het perron toen mijn trein vertrok.
mistakes.why: Dutch uses simply 'stond', not a form of 'zijn' with 'staan'.

contrast.dutch: Toen mijn trein vertrok, stond ik op het perron.
contrast.english: When my train left, I was standing on the platform.
contrast.note: Toen-clause first: 'stond ik' now leads the main clause.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Entering late and apologising are linked by one moment.

clauses.subject: Hij
clauses.why: Hij is first, so 'verontschuldigde' is second, with the reflexive 'zich' behind it.

clauses.subject: hij
clauses.why: The phrase 'te laat' stands before the joined verb 'binnenkwam', which closes the clause.

pat-toen-45.meaning: He apologised when he came in late.
pat-toen-45.order: The main clause carries the reflexive 'zich' right behind the verb. The toen-clause then says when, with 'te laat' before the joined verb 'binnenkwam'.
pat-toen-45.forms: zich verontschuldigen > verontschuldigde zich. binnenkomen > binnenkwam. 'Te laat' = too late.
pat-toen-45.compare: English 'apologised' has no reflexive. Dutch 'zich verontschuldigen' literally excuses oneself.

mistakes.wrong: Hij verontschuldigde toen hij te laat binnenkwam.
mistakes.right: Hij verontschuldigde zich toen hij te laat binnenkwam.
mistakes.why: The reflexive 'zich' is required: 'verontschuldigde zich'.

mistakes.wrong: Hij verontschuldigde zich toen hij te laat kwam binnen.
mistakes.right: Hij verontschuldigde zich toen hij te laat binnenkwam.
mistakes.why: The separable verb is written together at the end of the toen-clause.

contrast.dutch: Te laat binnenkomen vond hij vervelend, dus verontschuldigde hij zich.
contrast.english: He found coming in late annoying, so he apologised.
contrast.note: A different construction: an infinitive group as object fronted, then a causal clause.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The alarm interrupted the meeting at a specific point.

clauses.subject: Wij
clauses.why: Wij is first, so the plural 'zaten' is second; 'in de vergadering' is the place phrase.

clauses.subject: het brandalarm
clauses.why: The subject 'het brandalarm' comes first and the joined verb 'afging' closes the clause.

pat-toen-46.meaning: We were in the meeting when the fire alarm went off.
pat-toen-46.order: Dutch says that one 'sits in a meeting'. The interruption arrives in the toen-clause as a short subject plus verb.
pat-toen-46.forms: zitten > zat / zaten. afgaan > ging af / afging. 'Brandalarm' is a het-word.
pat-toen-46.compare: English 'were in the meeting' uses 'be'. Dutch uses 'zitten' (sit) for being in a meeting.

mistakes.wrong: Wij zaten in de vergadering toen het brandalarm ging af.
mistakes.right: Wij zaten in de vergadering toen het brandalarm afging.
mistakes.why: The separable verb 'afgaan' is joined at the end of the toen-clause.

mistakes.wrong: Wij zat in de vergadering toen het brandalarm afging.
mistakes.right: Wij zaten in de vergadering toen het brandalarm afging.
mistakes.why: Plural 'wij' needs the plural past 'zaten'.

contrast.dutch: Midden in de vergadering ging het brandalarm af.
contrast.english: In the middle of the meeting the fire alarm went off.
contrast.note: A fronted phrase replaces the toen-clause, and the verb splits again: 'ging ... af'.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The phone ringing at night startled me at that moment.

clauses.subject: Ik
clauses.why: Ik is first, so 'schrok' is second; the clause is short and complete.

clauses.text: toen de telefoon midden in de nacht ging
clauses.subject: de telefoon
clauses.why: The phrase 'midden in de nacht' stands before the finite verb 'ging' (rang), which closes the clause.

pat-toen-47.meaning: I was startled when the phone rang in the middle of the night.
pat-toen-47.order: Dutch uses 'ging' for a phone ringing, literally 'went'. The time phrase 'midden in de nacht' sits between subject and verb.
pat-toen-47.forms: schrikken > schrok. gaan > ging (here: ring). 'Midden in de nacht' = in the middle of the night.
pat-toen-47.compare: English 'rang' is a verb on its own. Dutch uses 'gaan' for a phone or a bell.

mistakes.wrong: Ik schrok toen de telefoon ging midden in de nacht.
mistakes.right: Ik schrok toen de telefoon midden in de nacht ging.
mistakes.why: The time phrase goes before the verb at the end of the toen-clause.

mistakes.wrong: Ik schrikte toen de telefoon midden in de nacht ging.
mistakes.right: Ik schrok toen de telefoon midden in de nacht ging.
mistakes.why: 'Schrikken' is irregular; the past is 'schrok'.

contrast.dutch: Midden in de nacht ging de telefoon en ik schrok.
contrast.english: In the middle of the night the phone rang and I was startled.
contrast.note: Two main clauses link the events in order without 'toen'.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The bill triggered the anger at one moment.

clauses.subject: De klant
clauses.why: 'De klant' is first, so 'werd' is second; 'boos' (angry) is the predicate.

clauses.subject: hij
clauses.why: The object 'de rekening' stands before the finite verb 'zag', which closes the clause.

pat-toen-48.meaning: The customer got angry when he saw the bill.
pat-toen-48.order: Cause and effect are reversed compared with a toen-first sentence: the anger is stated first, the seeing of the bill second, with 'zag' closing the sentence.
pat-toen-48.forms: worden > werd. zien > zag. 'Rekening' is a de-word.
pat-toen-48.compare: English 'got angry' uses 'got'; Dutch 'werd boos' uses the past of worden, and the toen-clause ends with the verb 'zag' instead of 'saw the bill'.

mistakes.wrong: De klant werd boos toen hij zag de rekening.
mistakes.right: De klant werd boos toen hij de rekening zag.
mistakes.why: The finite verb goes behind its object in the toen-clause.

mistakes.wrong: De klant werd boos toen hij de rekening zien.
mistakes.right: De klant werd boos toen hij de rekening zag.
mistakes.why: The toen-clause needs a finite past form, 'zag', not the infinitive 'zien'.

contrast.dutch: Bij het zien van de rekening werd de klant boos.
contrast.english: On seeing the bill the customer got angry.
contrast.note: A noun phrase replaces the clause, and the main clause inverts after the fronted phrase.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Your departure was already complete at the moment of the return call.

clauses.subject: Ik
clauses.why: Ik is first, so 'was' is second; 'al weg' (already gone) completes it.

clauses.subject: jij
clauses.why: The separable verb 'terugbellen' rejoins as 'terugbelde' at the end of the two-word clause.

pat-toen-49.meaning: I was already gone when you called back.
pat-toen-49.order: 'Al weg' shows that the departure was earlier than the call. The stressed 'jij' contrasts you with someone else.
pat-toen-49.forms: terugbellen: belt terug / belde terug / toen jij terugbelde. 'Weg zijn' = to be gone.
pat-toen-49.compare: English 'called back' is a phrasal verb. Dutch glues the particle on in a dependent clause.

mistakes.wrong: Ik was al weg toen jij belde terug.
mistakes.right: Ik was al weg toen jij terugbelde.
mistakes.why: The separable verb is written together: 'terugbelde'.

mistakes.wrong: Ik was weg al toen jij terugbelde.
mistakes.right: Ik was al weg toen jij terugbelde.
mistakes.why: The adverb 'al' goes before the predicate: 'al weg', not 'weg al'.

contrast.dutch: Jij belde terug, maar ik was al weg.
contrast.english: You called back, but I was already gone.
contrast.note: Two main clauses with 'maar' state the contrast without a time frame.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The laughter followed at once when the joke had been told.

clauses.subject: Zij
clauses.why: Zij is first, so the plural 'lachten' is second; 'hard' (loudly) closes it.

clauses.subject: de grap
clauses.why: The subject 'de grap' comes first; the passive group 'werd verteld' closes the clause with 'werd' before the participle.

pat-toen-50.meaning: They laughed loudly when the joke was told.
pat-toen-50.order: A passive in the toen-clause: 'werd verteld'. The speaker is not named. The finite verb is the second-to-last word.
pat-toen-50.forms: lachen > lachte / lachten. vertellen > verteld. 'Grap' is a de-word.
pat-toen-50.compare: English 'was told' is also a passive. Dutch 'werd verteld' follows the subject 'de grap'.

mistakes.wrong: Zij lachten hard toen de grap verteld werd was.
mistakes.right: Zij lachten hard toen de grap werd verteld.
mistakes.why: A passive uses only one auxiliary: 'werd verteld'.

mistakes.wrong: Zij lachten hard toen werd de grap verteld.
mistakes.right: Zij lachten hard toen de grap werd verteld.
mistakes.why: In the toen-clause the subject comes before the auxiliary.

contrast.dutch: Toen de grap werd verteld, lachten zij hard.
contrast.english: When the joke was told, they laughed loudly.
contrast.note: Toen-clause first: the main clause inverts to 'lachten zij'.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The neighbour's ring interrupted your reading.

clauses.subject: Ik
clauses.why: Ik is first, so 'zat' is second; 'te lezen' gives the progressive meaning 'sat reading'.

clauses.subject: mijn buurman
clauses.why: The subject 'mijn buurman' comes first and the joined separable verb 'aanbelde' closes the clause.

pat-toen-51.meaning: I was reading when my neighbour rang the bell.
pat-toen-51.order: 'Zitten te' + infinitive expresses being busy with something while seated. The short interruption follows in the toen-clause.
pat-toen-51.forms: lezen: zat te lezen. aanbellen: belt aan / belde aan / toen hij aanbelde. 'Buurman' is a de-word.
pat-toen-51.compare: English 'was reading' is a continuous. Dutch prefers 'zat te lezen' (sat reading).

mistakes.wrong: Ik zat lezen toen mijn buurman aanbelde.
mistakes.right: Ik zat te lezen toen mijn buurman aanbelde.
mistakes.why: The infinitive after 'zitten' needs 'te': 'zat te lezen'.

mistakes.wrong: Ik zat te lezen toen mijn buurman belde aan.
mistakes.right: Ik zat te lezen toen mijn buurman aanbelde.
