mistakes.why: The verb is joined in the dependent clause: 'aanbelde'.

contrast.dutch: Mijn buurman belde aan terwijl ik zat te lezen.
contrast.english: My neighbour rang the bell while I was reading.
contrast.note: 'Terwijl' presents two simultaneous processes instead of one interrupting the other.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Snow started at the moment of the climb.

clauses.subject: Het
clauses.why: Het is first, so 'begon' is second and 'te sneeuwen' follows as the infinitive group.

clauses.subject: we
clauses.why: The object 'de berg' stands before the joined separable verb 'opliepen', which closes the clause.

pat-toen-52.meaning: It began to snow when we walked up the mountain.
pat-toen-52.order: 'Beginnen te' + infinitive marks the start of the snow. The toen-clause names the climb, with the separable verb 'oplopen' rejoined as 'opliepen' at the end.
pat-toen-52.forms: sneeuwen: te sneeuwen. oplopen > liep op / opliepen. 'Berg' is a de-word.
pat-toen-52.compare: English 'walked up' is a phrasal verb. Dutch 'oplopen' has a particle that stays attached in a dependent clause.

mistakes.wrong: Het begon sneeuwen toen we de berg opliepen.
mistakes.right: Het begon te sneeuwen toen we de berg opliepen.
mistakes.why: With 'beginnen' the infinitive needs 'te'.

mistakes.wrong: Het begon te sneeuwen toen we liepen de berg op.
mistakes.right: Het begon te sneeuwen toen we de berg opliepen.
mistakes.why: The verb is written as one word at the end: 'opliepen'.

contrast.dutch: Toen we de berg opliepen, begon het te sneeuwen.
contrast.english: When we walked up the mountain, it began to snow.
contrast.note: Toen-clause first: the main clause inverts to 'begon het'.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: He was ready before the call; 'al' makes that order clear.

clauses.text: Hij had zijn jas al aan
clauses.subject: Hij
clauses.why: Hij is first, so 'had' is second; 'zijn jas al aan' is the object plus predicate 'aan'.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The object 'hem' stands before the finite verb 'riep', which closes the clause.

pat-toen-53.meaning: He already had his coat on when I called him.
pat-toen-53.order: 'Iets aanhebben' (to be wearing something) splits into 'had ... aan'. The toen-clause names the moment of the call.
pat-toen-53.forms: aanhebben: heeft aan / had aan. roepen > riep. 'Jas' is a de-word.
pat-toen-53.compare: English 'had his coat on' uses 'on'. Dutch uses the particle 'aan' at the end of the clause.

mistakes.wrong: Hij had zijn jas al aan toen ik riep hem.
mistakes.right: Hij had zijn jas al aan toen ik hem riep.
mistakes.why: The object 'hem' goes before the verb 'riep'.

mistakes.wrong: Hij zijn jas al aan had toen ik hem riep.
mistakes.right: Hij had zijn jas al aan toen ik hem riep.
mistakes.why: In the main clause the verb is second and the particle 'aan' is last: 'had zijn jas al aan'.

contrast.dutch: Toen ik hem riep, had hij zijn jas al aan.
contrast.english: When I called him, he already had his coat on.
contrast.note: Toen-clause first: 'had hij' leads the main clause.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The shutdown happened at the moment of the attempt to save.

clauses.subject: Mijn laptop
clauses.why: 'Mijn laptop' is first, so 'ging' is second and the particle 'uit' ends the clause.

clauses.text: toen ik het bestand wilde opslaan
clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The object 'het bestand' stands before the modal 'wilde', and the infinitive 'opslaan' closes the clause.

pat-toen-54.meaning: My laptop switched off when I wanted to save the file.
pat-toen-54.order: A modal and an infinitive end the toen-clause: 'wilde opslaan'. 'Uitgaan' splits in the main clause: 'ging ... uit'.
pat-toen-54.forms: uitgaan > ging uit. willen > wilde. opslaan: infinitive after the modal. 'Bestand' is a het-word.
pat-toen-54.compare: English 'wanted to save' stays in a chain. Dutch puts the modal before the infinitive at the end.

mistakes.wrong: Mijn laptop ging uit toen ik wilde het bestand opslaan.
mistakes.right: Mijn laptop ging uit toen ik het bestand wilde opslaan.
mistakes.why: The object goes before the modal group at the end.

mistakes.wrong: Mijn laptop uitging toen ik het bestand wilde opslaan.
mistakes.right: Mijn laptop ging uit toen ik het bestand wilde opslaan.
mistakes.why: In a main clause the separable verb splits: 'ging ... uit'.

contrast.dutch: Toen ik het bestand wilde opslaan, ging mijn laptop uit.
contrast.english: When I wanted to save the file, my laptop switched off.
contrast.note: Toen-clause first: 'ging mijn laptop uit' with the particle at the end.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Arriving is a single moment, and the meeting had begun before it.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The separable verb 'aankomen' rejoins as 'aankwam' at the end of the two-word clause.

clauses.subject: de vergadering
clauses.why: The auxiliary 'was' leads the main clause; the participle 'begonnen' ends it, so the past perfect surrounds 'de vergadering al'.

pat-toen-55.meaning: When I arrived, the meeting had already started.
pat-toen-55.order: Two past times: the arrival (simple past) and the earlier start (past perfect). 'Al' stresses that the start came first, and 'begonnen' stands at the end.
pat-toen-55.forms: beginnen > begonnen (participle, with zijn). The past perfect is 'was ... begonnen'. 'Vergadering' is a de-word.
pat-toen-55.compare: English 'had started' uses 'had'. Dutch picks 'zijn' for verbs of beginning and change: 'was begonnen'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik aankwam, had de vergadering al begonnen.
mistakes.right: Toen ik aankwam, was de vergadering al begonnen.
mistakes.why: 'Beginnen' forms its perfect with zijn here, so the auxiliary is 'was'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik aankwam, was de vergadering begonnen al.
mistakes.right: Toen ik aankwam, was de vergadering al begonnen.
mistakes.why: The adverb 'al' goes before the participle, which ends the clause.

contrast.dutch: De vergadering was al begonnen toen ik aankwam.
contrast.english: The meeting had already started when I arrived.
contrast.note: Main clause first: the past perfect now leads the sentence.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The technician's arrival is one moment; the fix had been done before it.

clauses.subject: de monteur
clauses.why: The subject 'de monteur' comes first and the finite verb 'arriveerde' closes the clause.

clauses.text: had ik het probleem al opgelost
clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The auxiliary 'had' leads the main clause; the participle 'opgelost' ends it after the object and 'al'.

pat-toen-56.meaning: When the technician arrived, I had already solved the problem.
pat-toen-56.order: The past perfect 'had opgelost' places the repair before the arrival. The object and 'al' come between the subject and the participle.
pat-toen-56.forms: arriveren > arriveerde. oplossen > opgelost (hebben). 'Monteur' is a de-word; 'probleem' a het-word.
pat-toen-56.compare: English 'had already solved' keeps 'had' next to the participle. Dutch splits them around the object.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de monteur arriveerde, heb ik het probleem al opgelost.
mistakes.right: Toen de monteur arriveerde, had ik het probleem al opgelost.
mistakes.why: The past perfect needs 'had', because the repair came before the arrival.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de monteur arriveerde, had ik opgelost het probleem al.
mistakes.right: Toen de monteur arriveerde, had ik het probleem al opgelost.
mistakes.why: The participle ends the clause, after the object and 'al'.

contrast.dutch: Ik had het probleem al opgelost toen de monteur arriveerde.
contrast.english: I had already solved the problem when the technician arrived.
contrast.note: Main clause first: the subject 'ik' leads and the auxiliary follows.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Your call came at one moment; she had left earlier.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The object 'haar' stands before the finite verb 'belde', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: ze
clauses.why: The auxiliary 'was' leads, then 'ze', 'al' and the participle 'vertrokken'.

pat-toen-57.meaning: When I phoned her, she had already left.
pat-toen-57.order: A past perfect with zijn: 'was vertrokken'. The pronoun 'ze' repeats the person that was 'haar' in the first clause.
pat-toen-57.forms: vertrekken > vertrokken (zijn). bellen > belde. 'Haar' is the object, 'ze' the unstressed subject.
pat-toen-57.compare: English 'she had already left' uses 'had'. Dutch uses 'zijn' with verbs of movement: 'was vertrokken'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik haar belde, had ze al vertrokken.
mistakes.right: Toen ik haar belde, was ze al vertrokken.
mistakes.why: Verbs of leaving form the perfect with zijn: 'was vertrokken'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik haar belde, ze was al vertrokken.
mistakes.right: Toen ik haar belde, was ze al vertrokken.
mistakes.why: After the comma the auxiliary leads: 'was ze'.

contrast.dutch: Ze was al vertrokken toen ik haar belde.
contrast.english: She had already left when I phoned her.
contrast.note: Main clause first, with the auxiliary second.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The mail arriving is one moment; nobody had noticed the fault before.

clauses.subject: de mail
clauses.why: The separable verb 'binnenkomen' rejoins as 'binnenkwam' at the end of the clause.

clauses.text: had niemand de storing nog opgemerkt
clauses.subject: niemand
clauses.why: The auxiliary 'had' leads, then 'niemand', the object 'de storing', 'nog' and the participle 'opgemerkt'.

pat-toen-58.meaning: When the email arrived, nobody had noticed the outage yet.
pat-toen-58.order: 'Nog' with the negative subject 'niemand' means 'not yet'. The participle 'opgemerkt' ends the main clause, behind the object, so the fault comes before the verb.
pat-toen-58.forms: binnenkomen > binnenkwam. opmerken > opgemerkt (separable participle). 'Mail' is a de-word.
pat-toen-58.compare: English 'nobody had noticed yet' keeps 'yet' last. Dutch puts 'nog' before the participle.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de mail binnenkwam, niemand had de storing nog opgemerkt.
mistakes.right: Toen de mail binnenkwam, had niemand de storing nog opgemerkt.
mistakes.why: After the comma the auxiliary leads: 'had niemand'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de mail binnenkwam, had niemand de storing nog opmerken.
mistakes.right: Toen de mail binnenkwam, had niemand de storing nog opgemerkt.
mistakes.why: The perfect needs the participle 'opgemerkt', not an infinitive.

contrast.dutch: Niemand had de storing nog opgemerkt toen de mail binnenkwam.
contrast.english: Nobody had noticed the outage yet when the email arrived.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, 'niemand' leads and 'binnenkwam' ends the toen-clause at the close.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Entering the room is one moment; the lesson had started earlier.

clauses.subject: wij
clauses.why: The object 'het lokaal' stands before the plural joined verb 'binnenkwamen'.

clauses.subject: de les
clauses.why: The auxiliary 'was' leads, then 'de les', 'al' and the participle 'begonnen'.

pat-toen-59.meaning: When we entered the classroom, the lesson had already begun.
pat-toen-59.order: Same shape as 'Toen ik aankwam, was de vergadering al begonnen', but with an object in the toen-clause. 'Binnenkomen' takes a direct object here.
pat-toen-59.forms: binnenkomen > binnenkwamen (plural). beginnen > begonnen. 'Lokaal' is a het-word.
pat-toen-59.compare: English 'entered' takes a direct object without a preposition, as Dutch 'binnenkomen' does in this use.

mistakes.wrong: Toen wij het lokaal binnenkwam, was de les al begonnen.
mistakes.right: Toen wij het lokaal binnenkwamen, was de les al begonnen.
mistakes.why: Plural 'wij' needs the plural past 'binnenkwamen'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen wij het lokaal binnenkwamen, was de les begonnen al.
mistakes.right: Toen wij het lokaal binnenkwamen, was de les al begonnen.
mistakes.why: 'Al' goes before the participle 'begonnen'.

contrast.dutch: De les was al begonnen toen wij het lokaal binnenkwamen.
contrast.english: The lesson had already begun when we entered the classroom.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, 'de les' leads and the toen-clause with the object 'het lokaal' closes the sentence.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Getting home was one moment, and it was already dark by then.

clauses.subject: Het
clauses.why: Het is first, so 'was' is second; 'al donker' (already dark) is the predicate.

clauses.subject: we
clauses.why: The adverb 'eindelijk' stands between the subject and the joined verb 'thuiskwamen', which closes the clause.

pat-toen-60.meaning: It was already dark when we finally got home.
pat-toen-60.order: 'Eindelijk' (finally) expresses a long wait. The main clause describes the scene; the toen-clause gives the moment of the arrival.
pat-toen-60.forms: thuiskomen > thuiskwamen (plural). 'Donker zijn' = to be dark. 'Eindelijk' = finally.
pat-toen-60.compare: English 'finally got home' separates 'home' from the verb. Dutch keeps 'thuiskwamen' as one word at the end.

mistakes.wrong: Het was al donker toen we eindelijk kwamen thuis.
mistakes.right: Het was al donker toen we eindelijk thuiskwamen.
mistakes.why: The separable verb is written together at the end: 'thuiskwamen'.

mistakes.wrong: Het al was donker toen we eindelijk thuiskwamen.
mistakes.right: Het was al donker toen we eindelijk thuiskwamen.
mistakes.why: In the main clause the finite verb is second: 'was al donker'.

contrast.dutch: Toen we eindelijk thuiskwamen, was het al donker.
contrast.english: When we finally got home, it was already dark.
contrast.note: Toen-clause first: 'was het al donker' with inversion.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The shop being closed was a state that already held at the moment of arrival.

clauses.subject: De bakker
clauses.why: 'De bakker' is first, so 'was' is second; 'al dicht' (already closed) is the predicate.

clauses.text: toen ik bij de winkel aankwam
clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The place phrase 'bij de winkel' stands before the joined verb 'aankwam', which closes the clause.

pat-toen-61.meaning: The baker was already closed when I got to the shop.
pat-toen-61.order: 'De bakker' means the baker's shop. The state 'al dicht' came before the arrival. The toen-clause carries a place phrase.
pat-toen-61.forms: aankomen > aankwam. 'Dicht zijn' = to be closed. 'Bakker' can mean the person or the shop.
pat-toen-61.compare: English 'the baker's' needs a possessive for the shop. Dutch 'de bakker' can name the shop directly.

mistakes.wrong: De bakker was al dicht toen ik aankwam bij de winkel.
mistakes.right: De bakker was al dicht toen ik bij de winkel aankwam.
mistakes.why: The place phrase goes before the final verb 'aankwam'.

mistakes.wrong: De bakker was al toen dicht ik bij de winkel aankwam.
mistakes.right: De bakker was al dicht toen ik bij de winkel aankwam.
mistakes.why: The predicate 'dicht' stays in the main clause, before the conjunction.

contrast.dutch: Toen ik bij de winkel aankwam, was de bakker al dicht.
contrast.english: When I got to the shop, the baker was already closed.
contrast.note: Toen-clause first: 'was de bakker al dicht'.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The completion of the update is one moment; the users had gone before it.

clauses.subject: de update
clauses.why: The predicate 'klaar' stands before the finite verb 'was', which closes the clause.

clauses.text: hadden de gebruikers het systeem al verlaten
clauses.subject: de gebruikers
clauses.why: The plural auxiliary 'hadden' leads, then 'de gebruikers', the object, 'al' and the participle 'verlaten'.

pat-toen-62.meaning: When the update was ready, the users had already left the system.
pat-toen-62.order: Plural subject, plural auxiliary: 'hadden'. The object 'het systeem' precedes 'al verlaten', which closes the main clause.
pat-toen-62.forms: verlaten > verlaten (the participle equals the infinitive). hebben > had/hadden. 'Gebruikers' is plural.
pat-toen-62.compare: English 'had left' is the same for any subject. Dutch needs the plural 'hadden' for 'de gebruikers'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de update klaar was, had de gebruikers het systeem al verlaten.
mistakes.right: Toen de update klaar was, hadden de gebruikers het systeem al verlaten.
mistakes.why: The plural subject needs the plural auxiliary 'hadden'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de update klaar was, hadden de gebruikers het systeem al verlaat.
mistakes.right: Toen de update klaar was, hadden de gebruikers het systeem al verlaten.
mistakes.why: The participle is 'verlaten', identical to the infinitive.

contrast.dutch: De gebruikers hadden het systeem al verlaten toen de update klaar was.
contrast.english: The users had already left the system when the update was ready.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, the plural subject 'de gebruikers' leads and the toen-clause ends the sentence with 'was'.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Getting home yesterday is one moment; the perfect tense in the main clause is the natural spoken choice.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The time word 'gisteren' stands before the joined verb 'thuiskwam', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The auxiliary 'heb' leads, then 'ik', the adverb 'meteen' and the participle 'gekookt'.

pat-toen-63.meaning: When I got home yesterday, I cooked straight away.
pat-toen-63.order: In speech the toen-clause is often in the simple past and the main clause in the perfect. The perfect stresses the result of the action.
pat-toen-63.forms: koken > gekookt (hebben). thuiskomen > thuiskwam. 'Gisteren' marks a finished moment.
pat-toen-63.compare: English mixes tenses less: 'I cooked straight away'. Dutch speech often says 'heb ik gekookt'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik gisteren thuiskwam, ik heb meteen gekookt.
mistakes.right: Toen ik gisteren thuiskwam, heb ik meteen gekookt.
mistakes.why: The auxiliary leads after the comma: 'heb ik'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik gisteren thuiskwam, heb ik meteen gekoken.
mistakes.right: Toen ik gisteren thuiskwam, heb ik meteen gekookt.
mistakes.why: The participle of 'koken' is 'gekookt', formed with ge- and -t, not 'gekoken'.

contrast.dutch: Toen ik gisteren thuiskwam, kookte ik meteen.
contrast.english: When I got home yesterday, I cooked straight away.
contrast.note: The simple past works too and sounds more written.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: One ringing is one moment, and picking up was the answer to it.

clauses.subject: de telefoon
clauses.why: The ringing phone is a short subject plus verb: 'de telefoon' first, and the finite verb 'ging' (rang) ends the clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The auxiliary 'heb' leads, then 'ik', and the participle 'opgenomen' of the separable verb 'opnemen' ends it.

pat-toen-64.meaning: When the phone rang, I picked up.
pat-toen-64.order: 'Opnemen' (pick up) forms the participle 'opgenomen' with ge- between the particle and the stem. The object is understood.
pat-toen-64.forms: opnemen > opgenomen. gaan > ging. 'Telefoon' is a de-word.
pat-toen-64.compare: English 'picked up' has a phrasal verb. Dutch needs the separable participle 'opgenomen'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de telefoon ging, heb ik genomen op.
mistakes.right: Toen de telefoon ging, heb ik opgenomen.
mistakes.why: The participle of 'opnemen' is one word: 'opgenomen'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de telefoon ging, ik heb opgenomen.
mistakes.right: Toen de telefoon ging, heb ik opgenomen.
mistakes.why: After the opening toen-clause, the auxiliary 'heb' takes the first place, then 'ik', so the pair 'heb ik ... opgenomen' wraps the sentence.

contrast.dutch: Ik heb opgenomen toen de telefoon ging.
contrast.english: I picked up when the phone rang.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, the perfect pair 'heb ... opgenomen' stays together and 'ging' ends the sentence.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Creating the ticket is a single act in which one slip happened.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The object 'het ticket' stands before the joined verb 'aanmaakte', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The auxiliary 'heb' leads, then 'ik', the object 'de bijlage' and the participle 'vergeten'.

pat-toen-65.meaning: When I created the ticket, I forgot the attachment.
pat-toen-65.order: Both verbs concern the same moment. The perfect 'heb ... vergeten' sounds natural when you talk about a result that still matters.
pat-toen-65.forms: aanmaken > aanmaakte. vergeten > vergeten (participle equals infinitive). 'Bijlage' is a de-word.
pat-toen-65.compare: English 'forgot' is the simple past. Dutch speech prefers the perfect 'heb vergeten' for a mistake you are reporting.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik het ticket aanmaakte, heb ik gevergeten de bijlage.
mistakes.right: Toen ik het ticket aanmaakte, heb ik de bijlage vergeten.
mistakes.why: The participle of 'vergeten' has no ge-, and it stands at the end.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik het ticket aanmaakte, ik heb de bijlage vergeten.
mistakes.right: Toen ik het ticket aanmaakte, heb ik de bijlage vergeten.
mistakes.why: The main clause after the comma opens with 'heb', and 'ik' follows it; the order 'ik heb' would be a main clause on its own.

contrast.dutch: Ik heb de bijlage vergeten toen ik het ticket aanmaakte.
contrast.english: I forgot the attachment when I created the ticket.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, the slip leads and the toen-clause adds the moment, ending in 'aanmaakte'.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The stay in Rotterdam is one episode in which you visited the harbour.

clauses.subject: we
clauses.why: The place phrase 'in Rotterdam' stands before the plural finite verb 'waren', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: we
clauses.why: The auxiliary 'hebben' leads, then 'we', the object 'de haven' and the participle 'bezocht'.

pat-toen-66.meaning: When we were in Rotterdam, we visited the harbour.
pat-toen-66.order: A period (the stay) frames a specific visit. The participle 'bezocht' has no ge- because of the inseparable prefix be-.
pat-toen-66.forms: zijn > waren. bezoeken > bezocht. 'Haven' is a de-word.
pat-toen-66.compare: English 'visited' is a simple past. Dutch uses the perfect 'hebben ... bezocht' in everyday speech.

mistakes.wrong: Toen we in Rotterdam waren, hebben we de haven gebezocht.
mistakes.right: Toen we in Rotterdam waren, hebben we de haven bezocht.
mistakes.why: 'Bezoeken' has the inseparable prefix be-, so the participle takes no ge-.

mistakes.wrong: Toen we waren in Rotterdam, hebben we de haven bezocht.
mistakes.right: Toen we in Rotterdam waren, hebben we de haven bezocht.
mistakes.why: The finite verb 'waren' goes behind the place phrase.

contrast.dutch: Toen we in Rotterdam waren, bezochten we de haven.
contrast.english: When we were in Rotterdam, we visited the harbour.
contrast.note: The simple past 'bezochten' reads more formally than the spoken perfect with 'hebben'.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Discovering the error is one moment; walking to the manager was the reaction.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The object 'de fout' stands before the finite verb 'ontdekte', which closes the clause.

clauses.text: ben ik naar mijn manager gelopen
clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The auxiliary 'ben' leads, then 'ik', the direction 'naar mijn manager' and the participle 'gelopen'.

pat-toen-67.meaning: When I discovered the error, I walked to my manager.
pat-toen-67.order: A verb of movement with a direction takes zijn in the perfect: 'ben gelopen'. The direction phrase stands before the participle.
pat-toen-67.forms: ontdekken > ontdekte. lopen > gelopen (zijn, with a direction). 'Manager' is a de-word.
pat-toen-67.compare: English 'walked' has no auxiliary choice. Dutch uses 'zijn' for movement to a place.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik de fout ontdekte, heb ik naar mijn manager gelopen.
mistakes.right: Toen ik de fout ontdekte, ben ik naar mijn manager gelopen.
mistakes.why: Movement toward a goal takes zijn: 'ben gelopen'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik de fout ontdekte, ben ik gelopen naar mijn manager.
mistakes.right: Toen ik de fout ontdekte, ben ik naar mijn manager gelopen.
mistakes.why: The participle goes to the end, behind the direction phrase.

contrast.dutch: Toen ik de fout ontdekte, liep ik naar mijn manager.
contrast.english: When I discovered the error, I walked to my manager.
contrast.note: The simple past tells the same story with one verb.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The rain is one episode in which the group stayed inside.

clauses.subject: het
clauses.why: The dummy subject 'het' comes first and the finite verb 'regende' closes the clause.

clauses.text: zijn we in het café gebleven
clauses.subject: we
clauses.why: The auxiliary 'zijn' leads, then 'we', the place phrase 'in het café' and the participle 'gebleven'.

pat-toen-68.meaning: When it rained, we stayed in the café.
pat-toen-68.order: The weather clause is only 'het regende'. In the main clause the perfect pair 'zijn ... gebleven' wraps the place phrase 'in het café' as it does for every movement or staying verb.
pat-toen-68.forms: blijven > gebleven (zijn). regenen > regende. 'Café' is a het-word.
pat-toen-68.compare: English 'stayed' has no auxiliary. Dutch uses 'zijn' with verbs of staying or becoming.

mistakes.wrong: Toen het regende, hebben we in het café gebleven.
mistakes.right: Toen het regende, zijn we in het café gebleven.
mistakes.why: 'Blijven' takes zijn as its auxiliary, so 'hebben ... gebleven' is wrong.

mistakes.wrong: Toen het regende, zijn we gebleven in het café.
mistakes.right: Toen het regende, zijn we in het café gebleven.
mistakes.why: The participle 'gebleven' ends the clause, behind the place phrase.

contrast.dutch: Toen het regende, bleven we in het café.
contrast.english: When it rained, we stayed in the café.
contrast.note: The simple past 'bleven' is also fine and sounds more like written storytelling.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Her departure is one moment; the farewell wave was my action at that moment.

clauses.subject: zij
clauses.why: The subject 'zij' comes first and the finite verb 'vertrok' closes the clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The auxiliary 'heb' leads, then 'ik', the object 'haar', 'nog' and the participle 'uitgezwaaid'.

pat-toen-69.meaning: When she left, I still waved her off.
pat-toen-69.order: The object 'haar' and 'nog' (one last time) sit between the auxiliary pair. The separable verb 'uitzwaaien' forms its participle as one word, 'uitgezwaaid'.
pat-toen-69.forms: uitzwaaien > uitgezwaaid. vertrekken > vertrok. 'Haar' is the object form.
pat-toen-69.compare: English 'waved her off' is a phrasal verb. Dutch 'uitzwaaien' is a separable verb with the participle 'uitgezwaaid'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen zij vertrok, heb ik haar nog gezwaaid uit.
mistakes.right: Toen zij vertrok, heb ik haar nog uitgezwaaid.
mistakes.why: The participle of 'uitzwaaien' is one word: 'uitgezwaaid'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen zij vertrok, ik heb haar nog uitgezwaaid.
mistakes.right: Toen zij vertrok, heb ik haar nog uitgezwaaid.
mistakes.why: The farewell clause must put 'heb' first and 'ik' second; the order 'ik heb' belongs to a main clause that opens the sentence.

contrast.dutch: Toen zij vertrok, zwaaide ik haar nog uit.
contrast.english: When she left, I still waved her off.
contrast.note: The simple past splits the particle: 'zwaaide ... uit'.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The failure of the test is one moment, and trying again was the group's response.

clauses.subject: de test
clauses.why: The subject 'de test' comes first and the finite verb 'mislukte' closes the clause.

clauses.subject: wij
clauses.why: The auxiliary 'hebben' leads, then 'wij', the object 'het', 'opnieuw' and the participle 'geprobeerd'.

pat-toen-70.meaning: When the test failed, we tried again.
pat-toen-70.order: 'Het' stands for the test. 'Opnieuw' goes before the participle 'geprobeerd', which ends the main clause. The plural 'hebben wij' leads after the comma.
pat-toen-70.forms: mislukken > mislukte. proberen > geprobeerd (hebben). 'Test' is a de-word.
pat-toen-70.compare: English 'tried again' puts 'again' last. Dutch puts 'opnieuw' before the participle.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de test mislukte, wij hebben het opnieuw geprobeerd.
mistakes.right: Toen de test mislukte, hebben wij het opnieuw geprobeerd.
mistakes.why: The auxiliary leads after the comma: 'hebben wij'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de test mislukte, hebben wij het geprobeerd opnieuw.
mistakes.right: Toen de test mislukte, hebben wij het opnieuw geprobeerd.
mistakes.why: 'Opnieuw' goes before the participle 'geprobeerd'.

contrast.dutch: Wij hebben het opnieuw geprobeerd toen de test mislukte.
contrast.english: We tried again when the test failed.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, 'wij hebben het opnieuw geprobeerd' leads and the toen-clause closes with 'mislukte'.

sense.label: toen = then (adverb, not a conjunction)
sense.why: Here 'toen' is a time adverb meaning 'then'; it begins the story step and has no second clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: 'Toen' takes the first slot, so the finite verb 'belde' is second and the subject 'ik' follows it.

pat-toen-71.order: One main clause only. Because the adverb 'toen' fills the first position, the verb stays second and the subject drops behind it, exactly as after 'daarna' or 'gisteren'.
pat-toen-71.forms: bellen > belde. 'Toen' as an adverb always refers to a point in the past; the present-tense counterpart is 'dan'.
pat-toen-71.compare: English 'Then I called' also inverts less visibly. Dutch always switches verb and subject after a fronted adverb.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik belde mijn collega.
mistakes.right: Toen belde ik mijn collega.
mistakes.why: As an adverb 'toen' does not send the verb to the end; the verb 'belde' stays second.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik belde, mijn collega.
mistakes.right: Toen belde ik mijn collega.
mistakes.why: 'Toen ik belde' would be a conjunction clause and leaves the sentence unfinished.

contrast.dutch: Toen ik belde, nam mijn collega op.
contrast.english: When I called, my colleague picked up.
contrast.note: With a comma and a second clause, 'toen' becomes a conjunction and the verb moves to the end.

sense.label: toen = then (adverb, not a conjunction)
sense.why: The adverb 'toen' tells what happened next; the verb stays second.

clauses.subject: de manager
clauses.why: 'Toen' fills the first slot, so the finite verb 'kwam' is second, followed by the subject 'de manager'.

pat-toen-72.order: The separable verb 'binnenkomen' splits here: 'kwam ... binnen'. A main clause keeps the particle at the very end, after the subject 'de manager'.
pat-toen-72.forms: binnenkomen > kwam binnen. 'Manager' is a de-word.
pat-toen-72.compare: English 'came in' keeps 'in' next to the verb. Dutch puts 'binnen' at the end of the clause.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de manager kwam binnen.
mistakes.right: Toen kwam de manager binnen.
mistakes.why: The subject must come after the verb in a sentence that starts with the adverb 'toen'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen binnenkwam de manager.
mistakes.right: Toen kwam de manager binnen.
mistakes.why: In a main clause the separable verb splits: 'kwam ... binnen'.

contrast.dutch: Toen de manager binnenkwam, werd het stil.
contrast.english: When the manager came in, it fell silent.
contrast.note: With a comma and a second clause, 'toen' is a conjunction and the separable verb is joined.

sense.label: toen = then (adverb, not a conjunction)
sense.why: This 'toen' is the adverb 'then' in a story; the light is the subject.

clauses.subject: het licht
clauses.why: 'Toen' fills the first slot, so 'ging' is second; the subject 'het licht' follows and the particle 'uit' ends the clause.

pat-toen-73.order: The separable verb 'uitgaan' splits: 'ging ... uit'. The sentence is a narrative step and stands alone, with the subject 'het licht' between verb and particle.
pat-toen-73.forms: uitgaan > ging uit. 'Licht' is a het-word.
pat-toen-73.compare: English 'went out' keeps its particle behind the verb. Dutch puts 'uit' at the end of the clause.

mistakes.wrong: Toen het licht ging uit.
mistakes.right: Toen ging het licht uit.
mistakes.why: After the fronted adverb, verb comes before subject: 'ging het licht uit'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ging uit het licht.
mistakes.right: Toen ging het licht uit.
mistakes.why: The particle 'uit' goes behind the subject, at the end.

contrast.dutch: Toen het licht uitging, was het donker.
contrast.english: When the light went out, it was dark.
contrast.note: With a toen-clause the separable verb is written together: 'uitging'.

sense.label: toen = then (adverb, not a conjunction)
sense.why: The adverb 'toen' tells when you saw her; the sentence has no subordinate clause.

clauses.text: Toen zag ik haar voor het eerst
clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: 'Toen' fills the first slot, so the finite verb 'zag' is second and the subject 'ik' follows it.

pat-toen-74.meaning: That was when I first saw her.
pat-toen-74.order: The time phrase 'voor het eerst' (for the first time) closes the sentence. The English translation needs 'that was when', but Dutch uses just the adverb.
pat-toen-74.forms: zien > zag. 'Voor het eerst' = for the first time.
pat-toen-74.compare: English often says 'that was when I first saw her' because 'then' cannot start a sentence like this. Dutch can start with 'Toen'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik zag haar voor het eerst.
mistakes.right: Toen zag ik haar voor het eerst.
mistakes.why: With the fronted adverb the order is verb, subject: 'zag ik'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen zag ik voor het eerst haar.
mistakes.right: Toen zag ik haar voor het eerst.
mistakes.why: The object 'haar' goes before the time phrase.

contrast.dutch: Toen ik haar voor het eerst zag, was ik verlegen.
contrast.english: When I first saw her, I was shy.
contrast.note: With a comma and a second clause 'toen' becomes a conjunction and 'zag' goes to the end.

sense.label: toen = then (adverb, not a conjunction)
sense.why: The adverb 'toen' marks the moment at which no option remained.

clauses.text: Toen had ik geen keuze meer
clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: 'Toen' fills the first slot, so the finite verb 'had' is second and the subject 'ik' follows it.

pat-toen-75.meaning: Then I had no choice left.
pat-toen-75.order: 'Geen ... meer' means no more. The negation is built into the object phrase 'geen keuze' with 'meer' behind it.
pat-toen-75.forms: hebben > had. 'Geen keuze meer' = no choice left. 'Keuze' is a de-word.
pat-toen-75.compare: English 'no choice left' uses 'left' for what remains. Dutch uses 'meer' (more), as in 'geen keuze meer'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen had geen keuze meer ik.
mistakes.right: Toen had ik geen keuze meer.
mistakes.why: The subject 'ik' directly follows the finite verb 'had'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik had geen keuze meer.
mistakes.right: Toen had ik geen keuze meer.
mistakes.why: With the adverb in first place, the verb is second.

contrast.dutch: Toen ik geen keuze meer had, gaf ik toe.
contrast.english: When I had no choice left, I gave in.
contrast.note: With a comma and a second clause, 'toen' becomes a conjunction and 'had' goes to the end.

sense.label: toen = then (adverb, not a conjunction)
sense.why: The adverb 'toen' moves the story to the point where things calmed down.

clauses.text: Toen werd het eindelijk rustig op kantoor
clauses.subject: het
clauses.why: 'Toen' fills the first slot, so 'werd' is second and the dummy subject 'het' follows it.

pat-toen-76.meaning: Then it finally became quiet at the office.
pat-toen-76.order: 'Rustig worden' expresses the change. The adverb 'eindelijk' sits before the predicate, the place phrase at the end.
pat-toen-76.compare: English 'became quiet' uses the verb 'become'. Dutch uses 'worden', the same verb that forms the passive.

mistakes.wrong: Toen het werd eindelijk rustig op kantoor.
mistakes.right: Toen werd het eindelijk rustig op kantoor.
mistakes.why: After the fronted adverb the verb comes second: 'werd het'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen werd het rustig eindelijk op kantoor.
mistakes.right: Toen werd het eindelijk rustig op kantoor.
mistakes.why: 'Eindelijk' stands before the predicate 'rustig'.

contrast.dutch: Toen het eindelijk rustig werd, ging ik naar huis.
contrast.english: When it finally got quiet, I went home.
contrast.note: With a comma and a second clause, 'toen' becomes a conjunction and 'werd' goes to the end.

sense.label: toen = then (adverb, not a conjunction)
sense.why: 'Toen pas' is a fixed adverbial pair meaning 'only then'; it fills the first slot.

clauses.text: Toen pas begreep ik de fout
clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: 'Toen pas' takes the first slot, so the finite verb 'begreep' is second and the subject 'ik' follows it.

pat-toen-77.meaning: Only then did I understand the error.
pat-toen-77.order: The English translation needs 'did' for the inversion. Dutch simply puts the verb second after 'toen pas'. 'Pas' emphasises that the insight came late.
pat-toen-77.forms: begrijpen > begreep. 'Pas' = only (in time). 'Fout' is a de-word.
pat-toen-77.compare: English 'only then did I understand' has the same inversion but with 'did'. Dutch does not need an auxiliary.

mistakes.wrong: Toen pas ik begreep de fout.
mistakes.right: Toen pas begreep ik de fout.
mistakes.why: The verb must come directly after the adverbial: 'begreep ik'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen begreep pas ik de fout.
mistakes.right: Toen pas begreep ik de fout.
mistakes.why: 'Toen pas' belongs together at the start.

contrast.dutch: Pas toen ik de fout zag, begreep ik het.
contrast.english: Only when I saw the error did I understand it.
contrast.note: Here 'pas toen' opens a toen-clause, so the verb 'zag' goes to the end.

sense.label: toen = then (adverb, not a conjunction)
sense.why: The adverb 'toen' leads to the moment when the customer finally answered.

clauses.text: Toen kregen we eindelijk antwoord van de klant
clauses.subject: we
clauses.why: 'Toen' fills the first slot, so the finite verb 'kregen' is second and the subject 'we' follows it.

pat-toen-78.meaning: Then we finally got an answer from the customer.
pat-toen-78.order: 'Eindelijk' expresses the long wait and sits before the object 'antwoord'. The source 'van de klant' closes the sentence after the object.
pat-toen-78.forms: krijgen > kreeg / kregen (plural). 'Antwoord' is a het-word. 'Van de klant' = from the customer.
pat-toen-78.compare: English 'from the customer' also follows the noun. Dutch 'van' is the equivalent of 'from' for the source here.

mistakes.wrong: Toen we kregen eindelijk antwoord van de klant.
mistakes.right: Toen kregen we eindelijk antwoord van de klant.
mistakes.why: After the fronted adverb the subject follows the verb: 'kregen we'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen kregen we eindelijk antwoord vanaf de klant.
mistakes.right: Toen kregen we eindelijk antwoord van de klant.
mistakes.why: The source is 'van de klant', not 'vanaf'.

contrast.dutch: Toen we eindelijk antwoord kregen, konden we beginnen.
contrast.english: When we finally got an answer, we could start.
contrast.note: With a comma and a second clause, 'toen' becomes a conjunction and 'kregen' goes to the end.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: A question can contain a toen-clause: it asks about what happened at one past moment.

clauses.subject: je
clauses.why: The question word 'Wat' opens, so the finite verb 'deed' is second and the subject 'je' follows it.

clauses.subject: de storing
clauses.why: The outage is a short subject plus verb: 'de storing' first, and the finite verb 'begon' ends the clause.

pat-toen-79.meaning: What did you do when the outage began?
pat-toen-79.order: The question has its own order (question word, verb, subject). The toen-clause at the end follows ordinary dependent order, ending in 'begon'.
pat-toen-79.forms: doen > deed. beginnen > begon. 'Wat' replaces the object that is asked for.
pat-toen-79.compare: English needs 'did' in the question. Dutch uses the plain past 'deed' directly behind the question word.

mistakes.wrong: Wat je deed toen de storing begon?
mistakes.right: Wat deed je toen de storing begon?
mistakes.why: In a direct question the verb comes right after the question word: 'Wat deed je'.

mistakes.wrong: Wat deed je toen begon de storing?
mistakes.right: Wat deed je toen de storing begon?
mistakes.why: In the toen-clause the finite verb goes to the end: 'de storing begon'.

contrast.dutch: Ik vraag me af wat je deed toen de storing begon.
contrast.english: I wonder what you did when the outage began.
contrast.note: In an embedded question both verbs move to the end of their clause.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: A where-question about the exact moment of the alarm.

clauses.subject: je
clauses.why: The question word 'Waar' opens, so the finite verb 'was' is second and the subject 'je' follows it.

clauses.subject: het alarm
clauses.why: The subject 'het alarm' comes first and the joined separable verb 'afging' closes the clause.

pat-toen-80.meaning: Where were you when the alarm went off?
pat-toen-80.order: The main clause is a standard 'waar' question: question word, verb, subject. The dependent clause keeps the separable verb joined at its end, 'afging'.
pat-toen-80.compare: English 'were you' also inverts, but Dutch uses 'was je' with the weak pronoun 'je'.

mistakes.wrong: Waar je was toen het alarm afging?
mistakes.right: Waar was je toen het alarm afging?
mistakes.why: The verb comes right after the question word: 'Waar was je'.

mistakes.wrong: Waar was je toen het alarm ging af?
mistakes.right: Waar was je toen het alarm afging?
mistakes.why: The separable verb stays together at the end: 'afging'.

contrast.dutch: Weet je nog waar je was toen het alarm afging?
contrast.english: Do you remember where you were when the alarm went off?
contrast.note: Wrapped in 'weet je nog', the inner question moves 'was' to the end of its clause.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: A question about who phoned during the meeting; 'er' fills the subject slot.

clauses.subject: Wie
clauses.why: The question word 'Wie' is itself the subject, so the finite verb 'belde' follows it directly, with the placeholder 'er' behind.

clauses.text: toen je in de vergadering zat
clauses.subject: je
clauses.why: The place phrase 'in de vergadering' stands before the finite verb 'zat', which closes the clause.

pat-toen-81.meaning: Who called while you were in the meeting?
pat-toen-81.order: When 'wie' is the subject, there is no inversion: verb right after 'wie'. The placeholder 'er' is typical for questions with an indefinite subject.
pat-toen-81.forms: bellen > belde. zitten > zat. 'Wie' = who (subject or object).
pat-toen-81.compare: English 'Who called?' has no placeholder; Dutch often adds 'er' after the verb.

mistakes.wrong: Wie er belde toen je in de vergadering zat?
mistakes.right: Wie belde er toen je in de vergadering zat?
mistakes.why: The verb comes right after 'wie': 'Wie belde er'.

mistakes.wrong: Wie belde er toen je zat in de vergadering?
mistakes.right: Wie belde er toen je in de vergadering zat?
mistakes.why: In the toen-clause the finite verb goes to the end, after the place phrase.

contrast.dutch: Wie heeft er gebeld toen je in de vergadering zat?
contrast.english: Who called while you were in the meeting?
contrast.note: A perfect-tense version of the same question, with 'heeft ... gebeld' around 'er'.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: A yes/no question about what someone already knew at one past moment.

clauses.subject: je
clauses.why: The finite verb 'Wist' opens the yes/no question, then the subject 'je', the object 'het' and 'al'.

clauses.subject: je
clauses.why: The object 'de uitnodiging' stands before the finite verb 'kreeg', which closes the clause.

pat-toen-82.meaning: Did you already know when you got the invitation?
pat-toen-82.order: A yes/no question starts with the verb. 'Het' stands for the whole content of the invitation, and 'al' asks about earlier knowledge.
pat-toen-82.forms: weten > wist. krijgen > kreeg. 'Uitnodiging' is a de-word.
pat-toen-82.compare: English 'Did you already know' needs 'did'. Dutch just starts with 'Wist je'.

mistakes.wrong: Je wist het al toen je de uitnodiging kreeg?
mistakes.right: Wist je het al toen je de uitnodiging kreeg?
mistakes.why: A real yes/no question starts with the verb: 'Wist je het al'.

mistakes.wrong: Wist je het al toen je kreeg de uitnodiging?
mistakes.right: Wist je het al toen je de uitnodiging kreeg?
mistakes.why: The object goes before the verb 'kreeg' at the end.

contrast.dutch: Wist je het al voordat je de uitnodiging kreeg?
contrast.english: Did you know before you got the invitation?
contrast.note: 'Voordat' asks about knowledge earlier than the receiving, 'toen' about the same moment.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: A how-question about the feeling at one moment.

clauses.subject: je
clauses.why: The question word 'Hoe' opens, so the finite verb 'voelde' is second, followed by the subject 'je' and the reflexive 'je'.

clauses.subject: je
clauses.why: The object 'de uitslag' stands before the finite verb 'hoorde', which closes the clause.

pat-toen-83.meaning: How did you feel when you heard the result?
pat-toen-83.order: 'Zich voelen' is reflexive, so 'je' appears twice: once as subject, once as reflexive pronoun. The toen-clause names the trigger.
pat-toen-83.forms: zich voelen > voelde zich. horen > hoorde. 'Uitslag' is a de-word.
pat-toen-83.compare: English 'feel' has no reflexive. Dutch 'zich voelen' does, here 'voelde je je'.

mistakes.wrong: Hoe voelde je toen je de uitslag hoorde?
mistakes.right: Hoe voelde je je toen je de uitslag hoorde?
mistakes.why: 'Zich voelen' needs its reflexive: 'voelde je je'.

mistakes.wrong: Hoe voelde je je toen je hoorde de uitslag?
mistakes.right: Hoe voelde je je toen je de uitslag hoorde?
mistakes.why: The object goes before the verb 'hoorde' at the end.

contrast.dutch: Hoe voel je je nu je de uitslag weet?
contrast.english: How do you feel now that you know the result?
contrast.note: The present tense and 'nu' replace the past moment.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: A question about the reaction at one moment of reading.

clauses.subject: de klant
clauses.why: The question word 'Wat' opens, so the finite verb 'zei' is second and the subject 'de klant' follows it.

clauses.subject: hij
clauses.why: The object 'de offerte' stands before the finite verb 'las', which closes the clause.

pat-toen-84.meaning: What did the customer say when he read the quote?
pat-toen-84.order: The noun subject 'de klant' follows the verb in the question, and the pronoun 'hij' in the toen-clause refers back to him. 'Las' ends the sentence.
pat-toen-84.forms: zeggen > zei. lezen > las. 'Offerte' is a de-word.
pat-toen-84.compare: English 'did ... say' needs 'did'. Dutch has 'zei' and swaps the order.

mistakes.wrong: Wat de klant zei toen hij de offerte las?
mistakes.right: Wat zei de klant toen hij de offerte las?
mistakes.why: In a direct question the verb comes after the question word: 'Wat zei de klant'.

mistakes.wrong: Wat zei de klant toen hij las de offerte?
mistakes.right: Wat zei de klant toen hij de offerte las?
mistakes.why: The object goes before the verb 'las' at the end.

contrast.dutch: Wat zegt de klant nu hij de offerte leest?
contrast.english: What does the customer say now that he is reading the quote?
contrast.note: Switching to 'nu' and the present tense makes the question about a reading that is still going on.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: A yes/no question about where someone was when the storm began.

clauses.subject: je
clauses.why: The finite verb 'Was' opens the yes/no question, then the subject 'je', 'al' and the predicate 'thuis'.

clauses.subject: de storm
clauses.why: The subject 'de storm' comes first and the finite verb 'begon' closes the clause.

pat-toen-85.meaning: Were you already home when the storm began?
pat-toen-85.order: A very short yes/no question: verb, subject, 'al thuis'. The toen-clause supplies the reference moment, so 'begon' ends the whole sentence.
pat-toen-85.forms: zijn > was. beginnen > begon. 'Thuis zijn' = to be at home.
pat-toen-85.compare: English 'Were you already home' also inverts. Dutch adds 'al' before the predicate.

mistakes.wrong: Je was al thuis toen de storm begon?
mistakes.right: Was je al thuis toen de storm begon?
mistakes.why: A real yes/no question puts the verb first: 'Was je al thuis'.

mistakes.wrong: Was je al thuis toen begon de storm?
mistakes.right: Was je al thuis toen de storm begon?
mistakes.why: The finite verb goes to the end of the toen-clause: 'de storm begon'.

contrast.dutch: Ben je al thuis nu de storm begint?
contrast.english: Are you already home now that the storm is beginning?
contrast.note: The present tense with 'nu' asks about the current moment.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: A why-question reproaching silence at one past moment.

clauses.subject: je
clauses.why: The question word 'Waarom' opens, so the finite verb 'zei' is second and the subject 'je' follows it.

clauses.text: toen ik je om hulp vroeg
clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The phrase 'je om hulp' (you for help) stands before the finite verb 'vroeg', which closes the clause.

pat-toen-86.meaning: Why did you say nothing when I asked you for help?
pat-toen-86.order: 'Vragen om' takes the preposition 'om' for what you ask for. The negative object 'niets' stands before the toen-clause.
pat-toen-86.forms: zeggen > zei. vragen > vroeg. 'Iemand om hulp vragen' = to ask someone for help.
pat-toen-86.compare: English 'asked you for help' uses 'for'. Dutch uses 'om': 'iemand om hulp vragen', and the verb 'vroeg' closes the toen-clause.

mistakes.wrong: Waarom je zei niets toen ik je om hulp vroeg?
mistakes.right: Waarom zei je niets toen ik je om hulp vroeg?
mistakes.why: The verb comes after the question word: 'Waarom zei je'.

mistakes.wrong: Waarom zei je niets toen ik je voor hulp vroeg?
mistakes.right: Waarom zei je niets toen ik je om hulp vroeg?
mistakes.why: 'Vragen' takes the preposition 'om', not 'voor'.

contrast.dutch: Waarom zeg je niets als ik je om hulp vraag?
contrast.english: Why do you say nothing whenever I ask you for help?
contrast.note: With 'als' and the present tense, the question refers to repeated occasions.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: A past period in Amsterdam: toen frames the whole stay, not one instant.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The place phrase 'in Amsterdam' stands before the finite verb 'woonde', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The finite verb 'werkte' leads, then 'ik' and the phrase 'bij een bank'.

pat-toen-87.meaning: When I lived in Amsterdam, I worked at a bank.
pat-toen-87.order: 'Toen' covers the whole period of living in Amsterdam. The job is a state during that period, so the simple past fits.
pat-toen-87.forms: wonen > woonde. werken > werkte. 'Bij een bank werken' = to work at a bank.
pat-toen-87.compare: English 'worked at a bank' uses 'at'. Dutch uses 'bij een bank' for an employer, and the main clause inverts to 'werkte ik'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik in Amsterdam woonde, ik werkte bij een bank.
mistakes.right: Toen ik in Amsterdam woonde, werkte ik bij een bank.
mistakes.why: After the comma the main clause opens with 'werkte ik'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik in Amsterdam woonde, werkte ik op een bank.
mistakes.right: Toen ik in Amsterdam woonde, werkte ik bij een bank.
mistakes.why: Dutch says 'bij een bank' for an employer.

contrast.dutch: Ik werkte bij een bank toen ik in Amsterdam woonde.
contrast.english: I worked at a bank when I lived in Amsterdam.
contrast.note: With the main clause first the period follows.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: A closed student period: toen frames the years in which she had a job.

clauses.subject: mijn zus
clauses.why: The subject 'mijn zus' comes first and the finite verb 'studeerde' closes the clause.

clauses.text: had ze een bijbaan in een café
clauses.subject: ze
clauses.why: The finite verb 'had' leads, then 'ze', the object 'een bijbaan' and the place phrase 'in een café'.

pat-toen-88.meaning: When my sister was studying, she had a part-time job in a café.
pat-toen-88.order: The whole stretch of studying is the frame. The object 'een bijbaan' (side job) is followed by the place phrase.
pat-toen-88.forms: studeren > studeerde. hebben > had. 'Bijbaan' is a de-word.
pat-toen-88.compare: English 'was studying' is a continuous. Dutch uses the plain past 'studeerde'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen mijn zus studeerde, ze had een bijbaan in een café.
mistakes.right: Toen mijn zus studeerde, had ze een bijbaan in een café.
mistakes.why: After the comma the main clause opens with 'had ze'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen mijn zus studeerde, had ze een bijbaan op een café.
mistakes.right: Toen mijn zus studeerde, had ze een bijbaan in een café.
mistakes.why: Dutch says 'in een café' for the place of work.

contrast.dutch: Mijn zus had een bijbaan in een café toen ze studeerde.
contrast.english: My sister had a part-time job in a café when she was studying.
contrast.note: With the main clause first the subject leads.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Childhood summers: toen frames a period, inside which the habit 'elke zomer' may occur.

clauses.subject: we
clauses.why: The predicate 'klein' stands before the plural finite verb 'waren', which closes the clause.

clauses.text: gingen we elke zomer naar zee
clauses.subject: we
clauses.why: The finite verb 'gingen' leads, then 'we', the time phrase 'elke zomer' and the direction 'naar zee'.

pat-toen-89.meaning: When we were small, we went to the sea every summer.
pat-toen-89.order: 'Toen' frames the period of being small. A repeated habit inside a closed period is still fine with 'toen', because the trigger is the period itself.
pat-toen-89.forms: zijn > waren. gaan > gingen. 'Naar zee' = to the sea.
pat-toen-89.compare: English 'went every summer' is a habit. Dutch also uses the simple past without 'used to'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen we klein waren, we gingen elke zomer naar zee.
mistakes.right: Toen we klein waren, gingen we elke zomer naar zee.
mistakes.why: The main clause opens with the verb: 'gingen we'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen we waren klein, gingen we elke zomer naar zee.
mistakes.right: Toen we klein waren, gingen we elke zomer naar zee.
mistakes.why: The plural verb 'waren' belongs behind the predicate 'klein'.

contrast.dutch: Als we klein waren, gingen we elke zomer naar zee.
contrast.english: Whenever we were small, we went to the sea every summer.
contrast.note: 'Als' would turn the sentence into a repeated pattern; 'toen' names the closed period.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The slow-internet era is a closed period that explains the habit of night downloads.

clauses.text: Toen het internet nog traag was
clauses.subject: het internet
clauses.why: 'Nog' and the predicate 'traag' stand before the finite verb 'was', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: we
clauses.why: The finite verb 'downloadden' leads, then 'we', the object 'alles' and the time phrase "'s nachts".

pat-toen-90.meaning: When the internet was still slow, we downloaded everything at night.
pat-toen-90.order: 'Nog' marks that the situation no longer holds. The apostrophe in "'s nachts" stands for the old genitive: of the night.
pat-toen-90.forms: downloaden > downloadde / downloadden. zijn > was. "'s nachts" = at night.
pat-toen-90.compare: English 'at night' is a prepositional phrase. Dutch uses the fixed genitive form "'s nachts".

mistakes.wrong: Toen het internet was nog traag, downloadden we alles 's nachts.
mistakes.right: Toen het internet nog traag was, downloadden we alles 's nachts.
mistakes.why: 'Nog' goes before the predicate; the verb 'was' ends the clause.

mistakes.wrong: Toen het internet nog traag was, we downloadden alles 's nachts.
mistakes.right: Toen het internet nog traag was, downloadden we alles 's nachts.
mistakes.why: The main clause opens with the verb: 'downloadden we'.

contrast.dutch: We downloadden alles 's nachts toen het internet nog traag was.
contrast.english: We downloaded everything at night when the internet was still slow.
contrast.note: With the main clause first the habit leads.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The first weeks at the company are a closed period in which you knew nobody.

clauses.text: Toen ik net begon bij dit bedrijf
clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: 'Net' stands before the finite verb 'begon'; the phrase 'bij dit bedrijf' trails behind it.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The finite verb 'kende' leads, then the subject 'ik' and the negative pronoun 'niemand'.

pat-toen-91.meaning: When I had just started at this company, I knew nobody.
pat-toen-91.order: 'Net' (just) before the verb signals a recent start. The phrase 'bij dit bedrijf' may follow the finite verb, so 'begon' is not the last word of the toen-clause.
pat-toen-91.forms: beginnen > begon. kennen > kende. 'Niemand' is a negative pronoun.
pat-toen-91.compare: English 'had just started' uses a past perfect. Dutch uses the simple past with 'net'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik net begon bij dit bedrijf, ik kende niemand.
mistakes.right: Toen ik net begon bij dit bedrijf, kende ik niemand.
mistakes.why: The main clause opens with the verb: 'kende ik'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik net begon bij dit bedrijf, kende ik geen niemand.
mistakes.right: Toen ik net begon bij dit bedrijf, kende ik niemand.
mistakes.why: 'Niemand' is already negative; 'geen niemand' doubles the negation.

contrast.dutch: Ik kende niemand toen ik net bij dit bedrijf begon.
contrast.english: I knew nobody when I had just started at this company.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, 'ik kende niemand' leads and the toen-clause about the first weeks closes the sentence.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Your grandfather's youth is a closed period before computers existed.

clauses.subject: mijn opa
clauses.why: 'Jong' (young) is the predicate before the finite verb 'was', so the verb ends this short clause about the grandfather.

clauses.subject: de computer
clauses.why: The finite verb 'bestond' leads, then 'de computer' and the closing 'nog niet' (not yet).

pat-toen-92.meaning: When my grandfather was young, the computer did not exist yet.
pat-toen-92.order: 'Nog niet' means not yet and closes the main clause after the subject. 'Bestaan' (to exist) is a state verb, so no participle is needed.
pat-toen-92.forms: bestaan > bestond. 'Computer' is a de-word. 'Opa' = grandpa.
pat-toen-92.compare: English 'did not exist yet' needs 'did'. Dutch uses 'bestond ... nog niet'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen mijn opa jong was, de computer bestond nog niet.
mistakes.right: Toen mijn opa jong was, bestond de computer nog niet.
mistakes.why: The main clause opens with the verb: 'bestond de computer'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen mijn opa was jong, bestond de computer nog niet.
mistakes.right: Toen mijn opa jong was, bestond de computer nog niet.
mistakes.why: The verb 'was' belongs behind the predicate 'jong'.

contrast.dutch: Er bestond nog geen computer toen mijn opa jong was.
contrast.english: There was no computer yet when my grandfather was young.
contrast.note: With 'er ... geen' the negation moves to the subject.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: One missed reply and one repeated call: the toen-clause names the trigger.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The negation 'niet' stands before the finite verb 'reageerde', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: hij
clauses.why: The finite verb 'belde' leads, then 'hij' and the phrase 'nog een keer' (once more).

pat-toen-93.meaning: When I did not respond, he called once more.
pat-toen-93.order: In the toen-clause the negation 'niet' stands right before the verb. The main clause ends with 'nog een keer', which expresses repetition.
pat-toen-93.forms: reageren > reageerde. bellen > belde. 'Nog een keer' = once more.
pat-toen-93.compare: English 'did not respond' needs 'did'. Dutch just puts 'niet' before the verb.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik reageerde niet, belde hij nog een keer.
mistakes.right: Toen ik niet reageerde, belde hij nog een keer.
mistakes.why: The negation goes before the finite verb at the end.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik niet reageerde, hij belde nog een keer.
mistakes.right: Toen ik niet reageerde, belde hij nog een keer.
mistakes.why: The main clause opens with the verb: 'belde hij'.

contrast.dutch: Hij belde nog een keer toen ik niet reageerde.
contrast.english: He called once more when I did not respond.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, 'hij belde nog een keer' leads and the toen-clause names the missed reply at the end.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The customer's absence at the agreed moment led to a decision to start.

clauses.text: Toen de klant niet kwam opdagen
clauses.subject: de klant
clauses.why: 'Niet' stands before the finite verb 'kwam', and the infinitive 'opdagen' ends the clause.

clauses.subject: we
clauses.why: The auxiliary 'zijn' leads, then 'we', the phrase 'zonder hem' and the participle 'begonnen'.

pat-toen-94.meaning: When the customer did not show up, we started without him.
pat-toen-94.order: 'Opdagen' (to show up) after 'kwam' forms a verb chain: 'kwam opdagen'. The perfect 'zijn ... begonnen' wraps the end of the main clause.
pat-toen-94.forms: opdagen: kwam opdagen (to turn up). beginnen > begonnen (zijn). 'Zonder hem' = without him.
pat-toen-94.compare: English 'did not show up' needs 'did'. Dutch uses 'kwam opdagen' with 'niet' before it.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de klant niet opdagen kwam, zijn we zonder hem begonnen.
mistakes.right: Toen de klant niet kwam opdagen, zijn we zonder hem begonnen.
mistakes.why: The finite verb 'kwam' comes before the infinitive 'opdagen'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen de klant niet kwam opdagen, hebben we zonder hem begonnen.
mistakes.right: Toen de klant niet kwam opdagen, zijn we zonder hem begonnen.
mistakes.why: 'Beginnen' takes zijn in this use: 'zijn ... begonnen'.

contrast.dutch: We zijn zonder hem begonnen toen de klant niet kwam opdagen.
contrast.english: We started without him when the customer did not show up.
contrast.note: With the main clause first the perfect pair stays at the front.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: A single forced choice is one moment, and the answer followed immediately.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The modal 'moest' leads the verb group, and the infinitive 'kiezen' ends the clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The finite verb 'nam' leads, then 'ik' and the object 'de goedkoopste optie'.

pat-toen-95.meaning: When I had to choose, I took the cheapest option.
pat-toen-95.order: The modal 'moest' with the infinitive 'kiezen' expresses obligation at that moment. The superlative 'goedkoopste' ends in -ste and takes -e again before a de-word.
pat-toen-95.forms: moeten > moest. nemen > nam. goedkoop > goedkoper > goedkoopste.
pat-toen-95.compare: English 'had to choose' uses 'had to'. Dutch uses the modal 'moest' plus infinitive.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik kiezen moest, nam ik de goedkoopste optie.
mistakes.right: Toen ik moest kiezen, nam ik de goedkoopste optie.
mistakes.why: The modal comes before the infinitive: 'moest kiezen'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen ik moest kiezen, nam ik de goedkoopst optie.
mistakes.right: Toen ik moest kiezen, nam ik de goedkoopste optie.
mistakes.why: The superlative before a de-word takes -e: 'goedkoopste'.

contrast.dutch: Ik nam de goedkoopste optie toen ik moest kiezen.
contrast.english: I took the cheapest option when I had to choose.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, the choice 'ik nam de goedkoopste optie' leads and the toen-clause adds the moment of deciding.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Her wish to know is the moment that triggered the full explanation.

clauses.subject: zij
clauses.why: The object 'het' stands before the modal 'wilde', and the infinitive 'weten' ends the clause.

clauses.subject: hij
clauses.why: The finite verb 'legde' leads, then 'hij', the object 'alles' and the particle 'uit' of 'uitleggen'.

pat-toen-96.meaning: When she wanted to know, he explained everything.
pat-toen-96.order: The modal 'wilde' and the infinitive 'weten' end the toen-clause. The separable verb 'uitleggen' splits in the main clause.
pat-toen-96.forms: willen > wilde. weten: infinitive after the modal. uitleggen > legde uit.
pat-toen-96.compare: English 'wanted to know' keeps 'to'. Dutch needs no 'te' after the modal 'wilde'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen zij het wilde te weten, legde hij alles uit.
mistakes.right: Toen zij het wilde weten, legde hij alles uit.
mistakes.why: After a modal the infinitive is bare, with no 'te'.

mistakes.wrong: Toen zij het wilde weten, hij legde alles uit.
mistakes.right: Toen zij het wilde weten, legde hij alles uit.
mistakes.why: The main clause opens with the verb: 'legde hij'.

contrast.dutch: Hij legde alles uit toen zij het wilde weten.
contrast.english: He explained everything when she wanted to know.
contrast.note: With the main clause first the particle 'uit' stays inside the main clause.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: Thunder is the moment that explains why sleeping failed.

clauses.subject: Ik
clauses.why: Ik is first, so the modal 'kon' is second, then 'niet' and the infinitive 'slapen'.

clauses.subject: het
clauses.why: The dummy subject 'het' comes first and the finite verb 'onweerde' closes the clause.

pat-toen-97.meaning: I could not sleep when there was a thunderstorm.
pat-toen-97.order: 'Onweren' is a weather verb with the dummy subject 'het'. The modal chain 'kon niet slapen' has the negation before the infinitive.
pat-toen-97.forms: kunnen > kon. onweren > onweerde. 'Slapen' stays an infinitive.
pat-toen-97.compare: English 'there was a thunderstorm' needs a noun. Dutch has the verb 'onweren'.

mistakes.wrong: Ik niet kon slapen toen het onweerde.
mistakes.right: Ik kon niet slapen toen het onweerde.
mistakes.why: The finite verb comes first: 'kon niet slapen'.

mistakes.wrong: Ik kon niet slapen toen het was onweer.
mistakes.right: Ik kon niet slapen toen het onweerde.
mistakes.why: Use the weather verb: 'onweerde'; the noun 'onweer' needs another structure.

contrast.dutch: Toen het onweerde, kon ik niet slapen.
contrast.english: When there was thunder, I could not sleep.
contrast.note: Toen-clause first: the modal 'kon' leads the main clause.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The update being installed is the moment that explains why the team had to wait.

clauses.subject: We
clauses.why: We is first, so the modal 'moesten' is second and the infinitive 'wachten' ends the clause.

clauses.subject: het systeem
clauses.why: The passive group 'werd bijgewerkt' closes the clause; the finite 'werd' comes before the participle 'bijgewerkt'.

pat-toen-98.meaning: We had to wait when the system was being updated.
pat-toen-98.order: A passive in the toen-clause: 'werd bijgewerkt' with the finite verb second to last. The main clause is a modal chain.
pat-toen-98.forms: moeten > moest / moesten. bijwerken > bijgewerkt. 'Systeem' is a het-word.
pat-toen-98.compare: English 'was being updated' is a continuous passive. Dutch uses only 'werd bijgewerkt'.

mistakes.wrong: We moesten wachten toen het systeem bijgewerkt werd was.
mistakes.right: We moesten wachten toen het systeem werd bijgewerkt.
mistakes.why: A passive has one auxiliary: 'werd bijgewerkt'.

mistakes.wrong: We moeten wachten toen het systeem werd bijgewerkt.
mistakes.right: We moesten wachten toen het systeem werd bijgewerkt.
mistakes.why: The story is in the past, so the modal needs 'moesten'.

contrast.dutch: Toen het systeem werd bijgewerkt, moesten we wachten.
contrast.english: When the system was being updated, we had to wait.
contrast.note: With the toen-clause first, the main clause inverts to 'moesten we wachten' and 'bijgewerkt' is no longer last.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The delivery arriving was a single moment when you were not at the office.

clauses.subject: Ik
clauses.why: Ik is first, so 'was' is second; 'niet op kantoor' places the negation before the place phrase.

clauses.subject: de levering
clauses.why: The subject 'de levering' comes first and the joined separable verb 'aankwam' closes the clause.

pat-toen-reuse-work-274.meaning: I was not at the office when the delivery arrived.
pat-toen-reuse-work-274.order: The negation 'niet' stands before the place phrase 'op kantoor'. The toen-clause is short and ends in the joined verb 'aankwam'.
pat-toen-reuse-work-274.forms: aankomen > aankwam. 'Levering' is a de-word. 'Niet op kantoor zijn' = not to be at the office.
pat-toen-reuse-work-274.compare: English 'wasn't at the office' contracts the negation. Dutch keeps 'niet' as a separate word before the place phrase.

mistakes.wrong: Ik was niet op kantoor toen de levering kwam aan.
mistakes.right: Ik was niet op kantoor toen de levering aankwam.
mistakes.why: The separable verb 'aankomen' is written together in the toen-clause.

mistakes.wrong: Ik was op kantoor niet toen de levering aankwam.
mistakes.right: Ik was niet op kantoor toen de levering aankwam.
mistakes.why: 'Niet' goes before the place phrase: 'niet op kantoor'.

contrast.dutch: Toen de levering aankwam, was ik niet op kantoor.
contrast.english: When the delivery arrived, I was not at the office.
contrast.note: Toen-clause first: the main clause inverts to 'was ik'.

pat-toen-reuse-work-274.situationNl: De bezorger kwam vorige week langs bij het bedrijf, maar jij werkte die dag ergens anders. Leg uit waar je niet was.

sense.label: toen = when (one past occasion)
sense.why: The technician's arrival is a single moment; the preparation had been finished earlier.

clauses.text: Ik had het voorbereidende werk al gedaan
clauses.subject: Ik
clauses.why: Ik is first, so the auxiliary 'had' is second; the participle 'gedaan' ends the main clause after the object and 'al'.

clauses.subject: de monteur
clauses.why: The subject 'de monteur' comes first and the joined separable verb 'aankwam' closes the clause.

pat-toen-reuse-work-321.meaning: I had already done the preparatory work when the technician arrived.
pat-toen-reuse-work-321.order: The past perfect 'had ... gedaan' shows that the work came before the arrival. The present participle 'voorbereidende' (preparing) works as an adjective.
pat-toen-reuse-work-321.forms: doen > gedaan. aankomen > aankwam. 'Voorbereidend' + -e before a het-word with the article 'het'.
pat-toen-reuse-work-321.compare: English 'had already done' keeps 'had' next to the participle. Dutch splits them around the object and 'al'.

mistakes.wrong: Ik had het voorbereidende werk al gedaan toen de monteur kwam aan.
mistakes.right: Ik had het voorbereidende werk al gedaan toen de monteur aankwam.
mistakes.why: The verb 'aankomen' is joined at the end of the toen-clause.

mistakes.wrong: Ik heb het voorbereidende werk al gedaan toen de monteur aankwam.
mistakes.right: Ik had het voorbereidende werk al gedaan toen de monteur aankwam.
mistakes.why: The earlier event needs the past perfect 'had', not the present perfect 'heb'.

contrast.dutch: Toen de monteur aankwam, had ik het voorbereidende werk al gedaan.
contrast.english: When the technician arrived, I had already done the preparatory work.
contrast.note: Toen-clause first: 'had ik' leads the main clause.

pat-toen-reuse-work-321.situationNl: Een technicus kwam gisteren voor een reparatie. Jij had van tevoren al veel gedaan. Vertel hoe ver je al was.
